09DEF29B70034661905687AACA7B765E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

266956AA3F7A482EA23C69729B90BFDD.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

95218A43170B4466BCB4D6B331B213C7.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.

F95AE5A5A4134B25AB3B0C74EA0BDF58.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

34543F6366A24B3A8EA2522F74944897.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

2F49474D54B14B898F459B6C6513FC1C.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

C70864F105B14E09911D7BE0963B2489.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented

61E03365F5CB401082E10475DCB50D0A.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

9E8D15D1218A41EBA5E9A9884572AB92.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

F0FF9A60348C4E4CA3C6A9E2B90548B9.description: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

05C49518DAB54F7DB91AD5A2A83E6E93.description: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

7763FD20B09246C18257CF3F59B3B272.description: Introduce a topic or thesis statement clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

B54F9E404E6145A4A89701DCD9168261.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content

47282924F4B44321A5AFAA4D05AAB5CE.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

BB89B8F0BD2342E59885C9FA2CF432B0.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

BCF0BAC8F3404670A43A6AFE2253F5C5.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), reasons, and evidence.

B27760D4079747238E02C1E766D3D7FC.description: Support claim(s) or counterarguments with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

9A8292C481674D6DA2424F04279FFA8A.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge and address alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

2AF69511429642E5B2CE2F22113E6A4A.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

8567F6035CC94B93B19708BD6E431433.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4D27C251D0BA443BAD983595392BF8CF.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

5573115113B245B087F0F62105A27286.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

4D6E6E6925584181B3B34D6A9E24D1CB.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

128F464684E641E39DEBE3A4FE0A0A92.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

ADB12DD7530A4092B5BD1C69CB8FF91E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

B82B9AFF61B84C09ABC0D9BC65A43EF3.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

D744317A13494A0F8B6A3CA9D27E86CA.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

571393C69E154C60B86C24F445A3703D.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

5E440F67E9CA41DABE7A4651064AC5C9.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

DEE46A8384E44882A24E5524A8EAECAD.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

29944841140F4F1C9E86688C28314028.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

FFEAF80BE55E47DE95FF4E894ABC92BE.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

22CA65C2D58249388B5A9836E82FE5B9.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

E959535DD6F8498A90021DB71628509B.description: Compare and contrast the information gained from experiments, simulations, video, or multimedia sources with that gained from reading a text on the same topic.

CF7929804A75472D9DC1EE1E9F98DCAD.description: Distinguish among facts, reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in a text.

BF7154B0FC8C45AC90601720245FAABC.description: Integrate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text with a version of that information expressed visually (e.g., in a flowchart, diagram, model, graph, or table).

CF606540BB5146D394294126A996551B.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text.

7A5EECB6E8694AEBA6F4B852019AABE1.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to an understanding of the topic.

A00584386103443E9E81D72FFA425613.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 6—8 texts and topics.

3463441F21DC4E838DA1896EB5419E4B.description: Follow precisely a multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks.

C30A64B9D9CE4318884838557E747513.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

F33E5D058A38470EA66467C4DCBFF361.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

CA2013AB942340E083FF6E3C600347BE.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

AE2FA6C18C1F49B5B572DE1817A9B7EB.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

723D4D63B6D94825B5027021A008E3B4.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

FA2207399D314247A956D3B20C47F545.description: Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same topic.

4692BFB4BFA549E88A8C9A5FCA3AF6AB.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

C943B314E0B84BA0A93473FEF1A534D4.description: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.

0E2E12158745466688AAC31C84C17C6A.description: Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's point of view or purpose (e.g., loaded language, inclusion or avoidance of particular facts).

6D4EB08761CF4ADFAD5CB43FECA81031.description: Describe how a text presents information (e.g., sequentially, comparatively, causally).

2DED65E8F1604A61A4A8044469B75627.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

BFEA29AA8A224D16AA14471EDFD6BA1E.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered).

BB3456F0234C4F4D909975C6A317D76F.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

0F4AEC56EFC448589A6F6E7880FB7818.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

294143420CB0449CB386A1BEE811D6DF.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

ECA7C65F5203452587BB7C3D7D3E9B76.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

EC320452A9FE4FB785F7023F705FAC9A.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D174F6903FA74346A94D119351532B26.description: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing different interpretations of facts.

227F5204650D49C9A5F97039D22D8F28.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.

C598B933F881449FA887FADE2AF297C2.description: Compare and contrast a text to an audio, video, or multimedia version of the text, analyzing each medium's portrayal of the subject (e.g., how the delivery of a speech affects the impact of the words).

E78B2E41374445BD993B9C9CB35B4D33.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.

9F2EAF9C723B4B938BBC3BC691160222.description: Analyze the use of text features (e.g., graphics, headers, captions) in public documents.

FBE5F419AA7842B48DAAF40365B86D55.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas.

824215F4F3F64E40A98EB62D50F063D0.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone. (See grade 7 Language standards 4–6 for additional expectations.)

B1FC3EDE98F94489A318115B03997A69.description: Analyze the interactions between individuals, events, and ideas in a text (e.g., how ideas influence individuals or events, or how individuals influence ideas or events).

755935DC359E4798B7E4B93DD8DF8F28.description: Determine two or more central ideas in a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

AA574773176543D09D38DFCC03241A9B.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

8344A875583C486493D56AA508610AC2.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

C327465C2B09436486E44DE074A28268.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4207273064134F7FBC380C4751189502.description: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history.

A6E73957709A495B8DAE232C5C88FDB0.description: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multimedia version, analyzing the effects of techniques unique to each medium (e.g., lighting, sound, color, or camera focus and angles in a film).

F19BC4C716EF42D8B7DA080088CAE219.description: Analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.

F7BA872274924D04842A9547CE65E5FC.description: Analyze how a drama's or poem's form or structure (e.g., soliloquy, sonnet) contributes to its meaning.

D326107A20E04A6CB83FDCE9E637A7F8.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of rhymes and other repetitions of sounds (e.g., alliteration) on a specific verse or stanza of a poem or section of a story or drama. (See grade 7 Language standards 4–6 for additional expectations.)

A655A5386B47448E864EE0DE68ACEDD1.description: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).

1D74F2D4C8AF4E5C977542BDCBA49E17.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

55FD418ABC444E939E3F82C6BEDCCEE3.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

57959A0BAD7A4246B5E27F60CEEE04A0.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

7D4B53D6C3EE4377A021C289F12B7E49.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4F51211BF5484524862B7ACDEF315B2A.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

40EBF93AA79545CB80259D169C077EF1.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

73CE5884C2BB4C1AB07D5970D8FBC36C.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

7F46DAE74EB94EDD85B391CAB91C50D7.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

B0211592BF974ADD93F871CD9767B2A9.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

0E2E7E973C0D4DE587B0E34EB227F028.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

E10F4DC409B9482BB48B84E5520687F6.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

BD4DBFDD9700420CB47E2510A253C752.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

51A445A61CAB4F4D812F9CE2460DA56A.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: History-Social Science Content Standards for California Public Schools, Kindergarten Through Grade Twelve

BE94E2A0DFE40131031D68A86D17958E.description: Explain foreign exchange, the manner in which exchange rates are determined, and the effects of the dollar's gaining (or losing) value relative to other currencies.

BE949820DFE40131031C68A86D17958E.description: Understand the changing role of international political borders and territorial sovereignty in a global economy.

BE9447E0DFE40131031B68A86D17958E.description: Compare the reasons for and the effects of trade restrictions during the Great Depression compared with present-day arguments among labor, business, and political leaders over the effects of free trade on the economic and social interests of various groups of Americans.

BE9402C0DFE40131031A68A86D17958E.description: Identify the gains in consumption and production efficiency from trade, with emphasis on the main products and changing geographic patterns of twentieth-century trade among countries in the Western Hemisphere.

BE93BCC0DFE40131031968A86D17958E.description: Students analyze issues of international trade and explain how the U.S. economy affects, and is affected by, economic forces beyond the United States's borders.

BE937570DFE40131031868A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between short-term and long-term interest rates and explain their relative significance.

BE931F30DFE40131031768A86D17958E.description: Define, calculate, and explain the significance of an unemployment rate, the number of new jobs created monthly, an inflation or deflation rate, and a rate of economic growth.

BE92AC30DFE40131031668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between nominal and real data.

BE925590DFE40131031568A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the aggregate economic behavior of the U.S. economy.

BE920B80DFE40131031468A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of international mobility of capital and labor on the U.S. economy.

BE91C5B0DFE40131031368A86D17958E.description: Discuss wage differences among jobs and professions, using the laws of demand and supply and the concept of productivity.

BE917E60DFE40131031268A86D17958E.description: Describe the current economy and labor market, including the types of goods and services produced, the types of skills workers need, the effects of rapid technological change, and the impact of international competition.

BE913590DFE40131031168A86D17958E.description: Understand the operations of the labor market, including the circumstances surrounding the establishment of principal American labor unions, procedures that unions use to gain benefits for their members, the effects of unionization, the minimum wage, and unemployment insurance.

BE90E340DFE40131031068A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the elements of the U.S. labor market in a global setting.

BE908560DFE40131030F68A86D17958E.description: Understand the aims and tools of monetary policy and their influence on economic activity (e.g., the Federal Reserve).

BE9034F0DFE40131030E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the aims of government fiscal policies (taxation, borrowing, spending) and their influence on production, employment, and price levels.

BE8FED90DFE40131030D68A86D17958E.description: Identify the factors that may cause the costs of government actions to outweigh the benefits.

BE8FA690DFE40131030C68A86D17958E.description: Understand how the role of government in a market economy often includes providing for national defense, addressing environmental concerns, defining and enforcing property rights, attempting to make markets more competitive, and protecting consumers' rights.

BE8F5DF0DFE40131030B68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the influence of the federal government on the American economy.

BE8CB230DFE40131030268A86D17958E.description: Discuss the economic principles that guide the location of agricultural production and industry and the spatial distribution of transportation and retail facilities.

BE8F1770DFE40131030A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the functions of the financial markets.

BE8EC9A0DFE40131030968A86D17958E.description: Explain the role of profit as the incentive to entrepreneurs in a market economy.

BE8E8550DFE40131030868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how domestic and international competition in a market economy affects goods and services produced and the quality, quantity, and price of those products.

BE8E3FF0DFE40131030768A86D17958E.description: Describe the effect of price controls on buyers and sellers.

BE8DFAE0DFE40131030668A86D17958E.description: Understand the process by which competition among buyers and sellers determines a market price.

BE8DB1F0DFE40131030568A86D17958E.description: Explain how prices reflect the relative scarcity of goods and services and perform the allocative function in a market economy.

BE8D5340DFE40131030468A86D17958E.description: Explain the roles of property rights, competition, and profit in a market economy.

BE8CF5D0DFE40131030368A86D17958E.description: Discuss the effects of changes in supply and/or demand on the relative scarcity, price, and quantity of particular products.

BE8C6D50DFE40131030168A86D17958E.description: Understand the relationship of the concept of incentives to the law of supply and the relationship of the concept of incentives and substitutes to the law of demand.

BE8C26C0DFE40131030068A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the elements of America's market economy in a global setting.

BE8BE190DFE4013102FF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the role of a market economy in establishing and preserving political and personal liberty (e.g., through the works of Adam Smith).

BE8B9360DFE4013102FE68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the role of private property as an incentive in conserving and improving scarce resources, including renewable and non-renewable natural resources.

BE8B3CC0DFE4013102FD68A86D17958E.description: Identify the difference between monetary and nonmonetary incentives and how changes in incentives cause changes in behavior.

BE8AF210DFE4013102FC68A86D17958E.description: Explain opportunity cost and marginal benefit and marginal cost.

BE8A9980DFE4013102FB68A86D17958E.description: Examine the causal relationship between scarcity and the need for choices.

BE8A5580DFE4013102FA68A86D17958E.description: Students understand common economic terms and concepts and economic reasoning.

BE7960E0DFE4013102C368A86D17958E.description: Students formulate questions about and defend their analyses of tensions within our constitutional democracy and the importance of maintaining a balance between the following concepts: majority rule and individual rights; liberty and equality; state and national authority in a federal system; civil disobedience and the rule of law; freedom of the press and the right to a fair trial; the relationship of religion and government.

BE89C7C0DFE4013102F868A86D17958E.description: Identify the successes of relatively new democracies in Africa, Asia, and Latin America and the ideas, leaders, and general societal conditions that have launched and sustained, or failed to sustain, them.

BE897860DFE4013102F768A86D17958E.description: Describe the ideologies that give rise to Communism, methods of maintaining control, and the movements to overthrow such governments in Czechoslovakia, Hungary, and Poland, including the roles of individuals (e.g., Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Pope John Paul II, Lech Walesa, Vaclav Havel).

BE892700DFE4013102F668A86D17958E.description: Identify the ideologies, causes, stages, and outcomes of major Mexican, Central American, and South American revolutions in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

BE88D9F0DFE4013102F568A86D17958E.description: Identify the forms of illegitimate power that twentieth-century African, Asian, and Latin American dictators used to gain and hold office and the conditions and interests that supported them.

BE8887D0DFE4013102F468A86D17958E.description: Describe for at least two countries the consequences of conditions that gave rise to tyrannies during certain periods (e.g., Italy, Japan, Haiti, Nigeria, Cambodia).

BE883FC0DFE4013102F368A86D17958E.description: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of federal, confederal, and unitary systems of government.

BE87EF90DFE4013102F268A86D17958E.description: Compare the various ways in which power is distributed, shared, and limited in systems of shared powers and in parliamentary systems, including the influence and role of parliamentary leaders (e.g., William Gladstone, Margaret Thatcher).

BE879450DFE4013102F168A86D17958E.description: Explain how the different philosophies and structures of feudalism, mercantilism, socialism, fascism, communism, monarchies, parliamentary systems, and constitutional liberal democracies influence economic policies, social welfare policies, and human rights practices.

BE874890DFE4013102F068A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the origins, characteristics, and development of different political systems across time, with emphasis on the quest for political democracy, its advances, and its obstacles.

BE870420DFE4013102EF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how public officials use the media to communicate with the citizenry and to shape public opinion.

BE86BE70DFE4013102EE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the roles of broadcast, print, and electronic media, including the Internet, as means of communication in American politics.

BE867720DFE4013102ED68A86D17958E.description: Discuss the meaning and importance of a free and responsible press.

BE862EB0DFE4013102EC68A86D17958E.description: Students evaluate and take and defend positions on the influence of the media on American political life.

BE85D850DFE4013102EB68A86D17958E.description: Understand the scope of presidential power and decision making through examination of case studies such as the Cuban Missile Crisis, passage of Great Society legislation, War Powers Act, Gulf War, and Bosnia.

BE8591C0DFE4013102EA68A86D17958E.description: Identify the organization and jurisdiction of federal, state, and local (e.g., California) courts and the interrelationships among them.

BE8549C0DFE4013102E968A86D17958E.description: Compare the processes of lawmaking at each of the three levels of government, including the role of lobbying and the media.

BE850420DFE4013102E868A86D17958E.description: Explain how public policy is formed, including the setting of the public agenda and implementation of it through regulations and executive orders.

BE84BC90DFE4013102E768A86D17958E.description: Discuss the Ninth and Tenth Amendments and interpretations of the extent of the federal government's power.

BE846F00DFE4013102E668A86D17958E.description: Discuss reserved powers and concurrent powers of state governments.

BE8415A0DFE4013102E568A86D17958E.description: Identify the major responsibilities and sources of revenue for state and local governments.

BE83A6E0DFE4013102E468A86D17958E.description: Explain how conflicts between levels of government and branches of government are resolved.

BE833F40DFE4013102E368A86D17958E.description: Students analyze and compare the powers and procedures of the national, state, tribal, and local governments.

BE82F570DFE4013102E268A86D17958E.description: Analyze trends in voter turnout; the causes and effects of reapportionment and redistricting, with special attention to spatial districting and the rights of minorities; and the function of the Electoral College.

BE82AA10DFE4013102E168A86D17958E.description: Discuss the features of direct democracy in numerous states (e.g., the process of referendums, recall elections).

BE824D10DFE4013102E068A86D17958E.description: Describe the means that citizens use to participate in the political process (e.g., voting, campaigning, lobbying, filing a legal challenge, demonstrating, petitioning, picketing, running for political office).

BE8201A0DFE4013102DF68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the roles of polls, campaign advertising, and the controversies over campaign funding.

BE81B570DFE4013102DE68A86D17958E.description: Discuss the history of the nomination process for presidential candidates and the increasing importance of primaries in general elections

BE816D40DFE4013102DD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the origin, development, and role of political parties, noting those occasional periods in which there was only one major party or were more than two major parties.

BE812880DFE4013102DC68A86D17958E.description: Students evaluate issues regarding campaigns for national, state, and local elective offices.

BE80DEA0DFE4013102DB68A86D17958E.description: Explain the controversies that have resulted over changing interpretations of civil rights, including those in Plessy v. Ferguson, Brown v. Board of Education, Miranda v. Arizona, Regents of the University of California v. Bakke, Adarand Constructors, Inc. v. Pena, and United States v. Virginia (VMI).

BE808CE0DFE4013102DA68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effects of the Court's interpretations of the Constitution in Marbury v. Madison, McCulloch v. Maryland, and United States v. Nixon, with emphasis on the arguments espoused by each side in these cases.

BE8047B0DFE4013102D968A86D17958E.description: Analyze judicial activism and judicial restraint and the effects of each policy over the decades (e.g., the Warren and Rehnquist courts).

BE7FFFF0DFE4013102D868A86D17958E.description: Understand the changing interpretations of the Bill of Rights over time, including interpretations of the basic freedoms (religion, speech, press, petition, and assembly) articulated in the First Amendment and the due process and equal-protection-of-the-law clauses of the Fourteenth Amendment.

BE7FB9E0DFE4013102D768A86D17958E.description: Students summarize landmark U.S. Supreme Court interpretations of the Constitution and its amendments.

BE7F7320DFE4013102D668A86D17958E.description: Explain the processes of selection and confirmation of Supreme Court justices.

BE7F1B60DFE4013102D568A86D17958E.description: Discuss Article III of the Constitution as it relates to judicial power, including the length of terms of judges and the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

BE7EBF10DFE4013102D468A86D17958E.description: Discuss Article II of the Constitution as it relates to the executive branch, including eligibility for office and length of term, election to and removal from office, the oath of office, and the enumerated executive powers.

BE7E6710DFE4013102D368A86D17958E.description: Identify their current representatives in the legislative branch of the national government.

BE7E23F0DFE4013102D268A86D17958E.description: Explain the process through which the Constitution can be amended.

BE7DDE50DFE4013102D168A86D17958E.description: Discuss Article I of the Constitution as it relates to the legislative branch, including eligibility for office and lengths of terms of representatives and senators; election to office; the roles of the House and Senate in impeachment proceedings; the role of the vice president; the enumerated legislative powers; and the process by which a bill becomes a law.

BE7D9A70DFE4013102D068A86D17958E.description: Students analyze the unique roles and responsibilities of the three branches of government as established by the U.S. Constitution.

BE7D5050DFE4013102CF68A86D17958E.description: Compare the relationship of government and civil society in constitutional democracies to the relationship of government and civil society in authoritarian and totalitarian regimes.

BE7D0300DFE4013102CE68A86D17958E.description: Discuss the historical role of religion and religious diversity.

BE7CB7A0DFE4013102CD68A86D17958E.description: Explain how civil society makes it possible for people, individually or in association with others, to bring their influence to bear on government in ways other than voting and elections.

BE7C5440DFE4013102CC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how civil society provides opportunities for individuals to associate for social, cultural, religious, economic, and political purposes.

BE7BE360DFE4013102CB68A86D17958E.description: Students evaluate and take and defend positions on what the fundamental values and principles of civil society are (i.e., the autonomous sphere of voluntary personal, social, and economic relations that are not part of government), their interdependence, and the meaning and importance of those values and principles for a free society.

BE7B8ED0DFE4013102CA68A86D17958E.description: Explain how one becomes a citizen of the United States, including the process of naturalization (e.g., literacy, language, and other requirements).

BE7B3610DFE4013102C968A86D17958E.description: Describe the reciprocity between rights and obligations; that is, why enjoyment of one's rights entails respect for the rights of others.

BE7AF2A0DFE4013102C868A86D17958E.description: Understand the obligations of civic-mindedness, including voting, being informed on civic issues, volunteering and performing public service, and serving in the military or alternative service.

BE7AABA0DFE4013102C768A86D17958E.description: Discuss the individual's legal obligations to obey the law, serve as a juror, and pay taxes.

BE7A6530DFE4013102C668A86D17958E.description: Explain how economic rights are secured and their importance to the individual and to society (e.g., the right to acquire, use, transfer, and dispose of property; right to choose one's work; right to join or not join labor unions; copyright and patent).

BE7A1760DFE4013102C568A86D17958E.description: Discuss the meaning and importance of each of the rights guaranteed under the Bill of Rights and how each is secured (e.g., freedom of religion, speech, press, assembly, petition, privacy).

BE79BFA0DFE4013102C468A86D17958E.description: Students evaluate and take and defend positions on the scope and limits of rights and obligations as democratic citizens, the relationships among them, and how they are secured.

BE790DC0DFE4013102C268A86D17958E.description: Understand that the Bill of Rights limits the powers of the federal government and state governments.

BE78C930DFE4013102C168A86D17958E.description: Describe the systems of separated and shared powers, the role of organized interests (Federalist Paper Number 10), checks and balances (Federalist Paper Number 51), the importance of an independent judiciary (Federalist Paper Number 78), enumerated powers, rule of law, federalism, and civilian control of the military.

BE788500DFE4013102C068A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Founding Fathers' realistic view of human nature led directly to the establishment of a constitutional system that limited the power of the governors and the governed as articulated in the Federalist Papers.

BE783FF0DFE4013102BF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the U.S. Constitution reflects a balance between the classical republican concern with promotion of the public good and the classical liberal concern with protecting individual rights; and discuss how the basic premises of liberal constitutionalism and democracy are joined in the Declaration of Independence as "self-evident truths."

BE77F7A0DFE4013102BE68A86D17958E.description: Discuss the character of American democracy and its promise and perils as articulated by Alexis de Tocqueville.

BE77A450DFE4013102BD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the influence of ancient Greek, Roman, English, and leading European political thinkers such as John Locke, Charles-Louis Montesquieu, Niccolò Machiavelli, and William Blackstone on the development of American government.

BE775DE0DFE4013102BC68A86D17958E.description: Students explain the fundamental principles and moral values of American democracy as expressed in the U.S. Constitution and other essential documents of American democracy.

BE76C480DFE4013102BA68A86D17958E.description: Principles of American Democracy and Economics

BE765AF0DFE4013102B968A86D17958E.description: Students construct and test hypotheses; collect, evaluate, and employ information from multiple primary and secondary sources; and apply it in oral and written presentations.

BE760970DFE4013102B868A86D17958E.description: Students evaluate major debates among historians concerning alternative interpretations of the past, including an analysis of authors' use of evidence and the distinctions between sound generalizations and misleading oversimplifications.

BE75C700DFE4013102B768A86D17958E.description: Students identify bias and prejudice in historical interpretations.

BE758240DFE4013102B668A86D17958E.description: Students distinguish valid arguments from fallacious arguments in historical interpretations.

BE753DE0DFE4013102B568A86D17958E.description: Historical Research, Evidence, and Point of View

BE74FA00DFE4013102B468A86D17958E.description: Students conduct cost-benefit analyses and apply basic economic indicators to analyze the aggregate economic behavior of the U.S. economy.

BE74AF40DFE4013102B368A86D17958E.description: Students analyze human modifications of landscapes and examine the resulting environmental policy issues.

BE745990DFE4013102B268A86D17958E.description: Students understand the meaning, implication, and impact of historical events and recognize that events could have taken other directions.

BE741200DFE4013102B168A86D17958E.description: Students interpret past events and issues within the context in which an event unfolded rather than solely in terms of present-day norms and values.

BE73C740DFE4013102B068A86D17958E.description: Students recognize the complexity of historical causes and effects, including the limitations on determining cause and effect.

BE7373C0DFE4013102AF68A86D17958E.description: Students show the connections, causal and otherwise, between particular historical events and larger social, economic, and political trends and developments.

BE72DE50DFE4013102AD68A86D17958E.description: Students relate current events to the physical and human characteristics of places and regions.

BE727D40DFE4013102AC68A86D17958E.description: Students use a variety of maps and documents to interpret human movement, including major patterns of domestic and international migration, changing environmental preferences and settlement patterns, the frictions that develop between population groups, and the diffusion of ideas, technological innovations, and goods.

BE7229F0DFE4013102AB68A86D17958E.description: Students analyze how change happens at different rates at different times; understand that some aspects can change while others remain the same; and understand that change is complicated and affects not only technology and politics but also values and beliefs.

BE71DB80DFE4013102AA68A86D17958E.description: Students compare the present with the past, evaluating the consequences of past events and decisions and determining the lessons that were learned.

BE7126E0DFE4013102A868A86D17958E.description: Historical and Social Sciences Analysis Skills

FE297D70DFE301319AA568A86D17958E.description: Critique dance works to improve choreographic structure and artistic presence.

FE2A7000DFE301319AA868A86D17958E.description: Defend personal preferences about dance styles and choreographic forms, using criteria-based assessment.

FE2A2150DFE301319AA768A86D17958E.description: Apply criteria-based assessments appropriate to various dance forms (e.g., concert jazz, street, liturgical).

FE291DF0DFE301319AA468A86D17958E.description: Describe how the qualities of a theatrical production contribute to the success of a dance performance (e.g., music, lighting, costuming, text, set design).

FE28B610DFE301319AA368A86D17958E.description: Description, Analysis, and Criticism of Dance

FE280DA0DFE301319AA168A86D17958E.description: Explain how dancers from various cultures and historical periods reflect diversity and values (e.g., ethnicity, gender, body types, and religious intent).

FE2531C0DFE301319A9968A86D17958E.description: Identify, analyze, and perform folk/traditional, social, and theatrical dances with techni-cal accuracy and appropriate stylistic nuances.

FE2609F0DFE301319A9B68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which folk/traditional, social, and theatrical dances reflect their specific cultural context.

FE24E3D0DFE301319A9868A86D17958E.description: Identify and perform folk/traditional, social, and theatrical dances with appropriate stylistic nuances.

FE2444B0DFE301319A9668A86D17958E.description: Historical and Cultural Context - Understanding the Historical Contributions and Cultural Dimensions of Dance

FE237E00DFE301319A9468A86D17958E.description: Perform a diverse range of works by various dance artists, maintaining the integrity of the work while applying personal artistic expression.

FE23EAF0DFE301319A9568A86D17958E.description: Perform works by various dance artists communicating the original intent of the work while employing personal artistic intent and interpretation.

FE2327E0DFE301319A9368A86D17958E.description: Perform original works that employ personal artistic intent and communicate effectively.

FE222B50DFE301319A9068A86D17958E.description: Teach to peers a variety of complex movement patterns and phrases.

FE2189F0DFE301319A8E68A86D17958E.description: Collaborate with peers in the development of complex choreography in diverse group-ings (e.g., all male, all female, people standing with people sitting).

FE21D820DFE301319A8F68A86D17958E.description: Collaborate with peers in the development of choreography in groups (e.g., duets, trios, small ensembles).

FE208160DFE301319A8B68A86D17958E.description: Notate dances, using a variety of systems (e.g., labanotation, motif writing, personal systems).

FE1FBE40DFE301319A8968A86D17958E.description: Use dance structures, musical forms, theatrical elements, and technology to create original works.

FE20E080DFE301319A8C68A86D17958E.description: Design a dance that utilizes an established dance style or genre.

FE200BD0DFE301319A8A68A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply basic music elements (e.g., rhythm, meter, tempo, timbre) to construct and perform dances.

FE1F6E20DFE301319A8868A86D17958E.description: Application of Choreographic Principles and Processes to Creating Dance

FE1ED070DFE301319A8668A86D17958E.description: Create a diverse body of works of dance, each of which demonstrates originality, unity, clarity of intent, and a dynamic range of movement.

FE1F2090DFE301319A8768A86D17958E.description: Create a body of works of dance demonstrating originality, unity, and clarity of intent.

FE1C9F20DFE301319A8068A86D17958E.description: Perform in multiple dance genres, integrating an advanced level of technical skill and clear intent.

FE1A2ED0DFE301319A7968A86D17958E.description: Apply a wide range of kinesthetic communication, demonstrating clarity of intent and stylistic nuance.

document.title: History-Social Science Content Standards for California Public Schools, Kindergarten Through Grade Twelve

BD89B6D0DFE40131009D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the components of California's governance structure (e.g., cities and towns, Indian rancherias and reservations, counties, school districts).

BD8971E0DFE40131009C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the structures and functions of state governments, including the roles and responsibilities of their elected officials.

BD891B30DFE40131009B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the similarities (e.g., written documents, rule of law, consent of the governed, three separate branches) and differences (e.g., scope of jurisdiction, limits on government powers, use of the military) among federal, state, and local governments.

BD88DB90DFE40131009A68A86D17958E.description: Understand the purpose of the California Constitution, its key principles, and its relationship to the U.S. Constitution.

BD889C50DFE40131009968A86D17958E.description: Discuss what the U.S. Constitution is and why it is important (i.e., a written document that defines the structure and purpose of the U.S. government and describes the shared powers of federal, state, and local governments).

BD885CB0DFE40131009868A86D17958E.description: Students understand the structures, functions, and powers of the local, state, and federal governments as described in the U.S. Constitution.

BD881D40DFE40131009768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of twentieth-century Californians on the nation's artistic and cultural development, including the rise of the entertainment industry (e.g., Louis B. Mayer, Walt Disney, John Steinbeck, Ansel Adams, Dorothea Lange, John Wayne).

BD87D510DFE40131009668A86D17958E.description: Describe the history and development of California's public education system, including universities and community colleges.

BD878450DFE40131009568A86D17958E.description: Trace the evolution of California's water system into a network of dams, aqueducts, and reservoirs.

BD872C60DFE40131009468A86D17958E.description: Describe the development and locations of new industries since the nineteenth century, such as the aerospace industry, electronics industry, large-scale commercial agriculture and irrigation projects, the oil and automobile industries, communications and defense industries, and important trade links with the Pacific Basin.

BD86E6E0DFE40131009368A86D17958E.description: Discuss the effects of the Great Depression, the Dust Bowl, and World War II on California.

BD86A1C0DFE40131009268A86D17958E.description: Describe rapid American immigration, internal migration, settlement, and the growth of towns and cities (e.g., Los Angeles).

BD865890DFE40131009168A86D17958E.description: Discuss immigration and migration to California between 1850 and 1900, including the diverse composition of those who came; the countries of origin and their relative locations; and conflicts and accords among the diverse groups (e.g., the 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act).

BD861380DFE40131009068A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Gold Rush transformed the economy of California, including the types of products produced and consumed, changes in towns (e.g., Sacramento, San Francisco), and economic conflicts between diverse groups of people.

BD85D2E0DFE40131008F68A86D17958E.description: Understand the story and lasting influence of the Pony Express, Overland Mail Service, Western Union, and the building of the transcontinental railroad, including the contributions of Chinese workers to its construction.

BD8585B0DFE40131008E68A86D17958E.description: Students explain how California became an agricultural and industrial power, tracing the transformation of the California economy and its political and cultural development since the 1850s.

BD8544B0DFE40131008D68A86D17958E.description: Discuss how California became a state and how its new government differed from those during the Spanish and Mexican periods.

BD8504B0DFE40131008C68A86D17958E.description: Study the lives of women who helped build early California (e.g., Biddy Mason).

BD84C390DFE40131008B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effects of the Gold Rush on settlements, daily life, politics, and the physical environment (e.g., using biographies of John Sutter, Mariano Guadalupe Vallejo, Louise Clapp).

BD847DD0DFE40131008A68A86D17958E.description: Compare how and why people traveled to California and the routes they traveled (e.g., James Beckwourth, John Bidwell, John C. Fremont, Pio Pico).

BD843B90DFE40131008968A86D17958E.description: Identify the locations of Mexican settlements in California and those of other settlements, including Fort Ross and Sutter's Fort.

BD83EBC0DFE40131008868A86D17958E.description: Students explain the economic, social, and political life in California from the establishment of the Bear Flag Republic through the Mexican-American War, the Gold Rush, and the granting of statehood.

BD839F10DFE40131008768A86D17958E.description: Discuss the period of Mexican rule in California and its attributes, including land grants, secularization of the missions, and the rise of the rancho economy.

BD835F70DFE40131008668A86D17958E.description: Describe the effects of the Mexican War for Independence on Alta California, including its effects on the territorial boundaries of North America.

BD831F00DFE40131008568A86D17958E.description: Discuss the role of the Franciscans in changing the economy of California from a hunter-gatherer economy to an agricultural economy.

BD82DC40DFE40131008468A86D17958E.description: Describe the daily lives of the people, native and nonnative, who occupied the presidios, missions, ranchos, and pueblos.

BD829070DFE40131008368A86D17958E.description: Describe the mapping of, geographic basis of, and economic factors in the placement and function of the Spanish missions; and understand how the mission system expanded the influence of Spain and Catholicism throughout New Spain and Latin America.

BD824470DFE40131008268A86D17958E.description: Describe the Spanish exploration and colonization of California, including the relationships among soldiers, missionaries, and Indians (e.g., Juan Crespi, Junipero Serra, Gaspar de Portola).

BD81E070DFE40131008168A86D17958E.description: Identify the early land and sea routes to, and European settlements in, California with a focus on the exploration of the North Pacific (e.g., by Captain James Cook, Vitus Bering, Juan Cabrillo), noting especially the importance of mountains, deserts, ocean currents, and wind patterns.

BD81A080DFE40131008068A86D17958E.description: Discuss the major nations of California Indians, including their geographic distribution, economic activities, legends, and religious beliefs; and describe how they depended on, adapted to, and modi°fied the physical environment by cultivation of land and use of sea resources.

BD816060DFE40131007F68A86D17958E.description: Students describe the social, political, cultural, and economic life and interactions among people of California from the pre-Columbian societies to the Spanish mission and Mexican rancho periods.

BD811EA0DFE40131007E68A86D17958E.description: Use maps, charts, and pictures to describe how communities in California vary in land use, vegetation, wildlife, climate, population density, architecture, services, and transportation.

BD80CDA0DFE40131007D68A86D17958E.description: Identify the locations of the Pacific Ocean, rivers, valleys, and mountain passes and explain their effects on the growth of towns.

BD805FE0DFE40131007C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the state capital and describe the various regions of Califor°nia, including how their characteristics and physical environments (e.g., water, landforms, vegetation, climate) affect human activity.

BD801380DFE40131007B68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between the North and South Poles; the equator and the prime meridian; the tropics; and the hemispheres, using coordinates to plot locations.

BD7FCEE0DFE40131007A68A86D17958E.description: Explain and use the coordinate grid system of latitude and longitude to determine the absolute locations of places in California and on Earth.

BD7F8680DFE40131007968A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate an understanding of the physical and human geographic features that define places and regions in California.

BD7F0930DFE40131007768A86D17958E.description: Students conduct cost-benefit analyses of historical and current events.

BD7EC340DFE40131007668A86D17958E.description: Students identify and interpret the multiple causes and effects of historical events.

BD7E7AC0DFE40131007568A86D17958E.description: Students identify the human and physical characteristics of the places they are studying and explain how those features form the unique character of those places.

BD7E3F50DFE40131007468A86D17958E.description: Students summarize the key events of the era they are studying and explain the historical contexts of those events.

BD7DC870DFE40131007268A86D17958E.description: Students distinguish fact from fiction by comparing documentary sources on historical figures and events with fictionalized characters and events.

BD7D8C40DFE40131007168A86D17958E.description: Students pose relevant questions about events they encounter in historical documents, eyewitness accounts, oral histories, letters, diaries, artifacts, photographs, maps, artworks, and architecture.

BD7D4EC0DFE40131007068A86D17958E.description: Students differentiate between primary and secondary sources.

BD7D0E70DFE40131006F68A86D17958E.description: Research, Evidence, and Point of View

BD7CC5B0DFE40131006E68A86D17958E.description: Students judge the significance of the relative location of a place (e.g., proximity to a harbor, on trade routes) and analyze how relative advantages or disadvantages can change over time.

BD7C8740DFE40131006D68A86D17958E.description: Students use map and globe skills to determine the absolute locations of places and interpret information available through a map's or globe's legend, scale, and symbolic representations.

BD7C48A0DFE40131006C68A86D17958E.description: Students explain how the present is connected to the past, identifying both similarities and differences between the two, and how some things change over time and some things stay the same.

BD7C0BD0DFE40131006B68A86D17958E.description: Students correctly apply terms related to time, including past, present, future, decade, century, and generation.

BD7BCDB0DFE40131006A68A86D17958E.description: Students place key events and people of the historical era they are studying in a chronological sequence and within a spatial context; they interpret time lines.

BD7B3A00DFE40131006868A86D17958E.description: Historical and Social Sciences Analysis Skills

document.title: Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools, Kindergarten Through Grade Twelve

F6AA3EC0DFE301318DA368A86D17958E.description: Work in pairs or small groups to achieve an agreed-upon goal.

F6A9ADD0DFE301318DA168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate respect for individual differences in physical abilities.

F6A96600DFE301318DA068A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate cues for movement and positive words of encouragement while coaching others in physical activities.

F6A8C500DFE301318D9E68A86D17958E.description: List the benefits of following and the risks of not following safety procedures and rules associated with physical activity.

F6A884D0DFE301318D9D68A86D17958E.description: Collect data and record progress toward mastery of a motor skill.

F6A84410DFE301318D9C68A86D17958E.description: Set a personal goal to improve a motor skill and work toward that goal in nonschool time.

F6A7BDC0DFE301318D9A68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate and utilize knowledge of psychological and sociological concepts, principles, and strategies that apply to the learning and performance of physical activity.

F6A77360DFE301318D9968A86D17958E.description: Differentiate the body's ability to consume calories and burn fat during periods of inactivity and during long periods of moderate physical activity.

F6A6D6A0DFE301318D9768A86D17958E.description: Explain why a particular stretch is appropriate preparation for a particular physical activity.

F6A68950DFE301318D9668A86D17958E.description: Identify flexibility exercises that are not safe for the joints and should be avoided.

F6A5C030DFE301318D9368A86D17958E.description: Describe the role of muscle strength and proper lifting in the prevention of back injuries.

F6A57560DFE301318D9268A86D17958E.description: Describe and demonstrate how to relieve a muscle cramp.

F6A53440DFE301318D9168A86D17958E.description: Name and locate the major muscles of the body.

F6A4F190DFE301318D9068A86D17958E.description: Identify which muscles are used in performing muscular endurance activities.

F6A60810DFE301318D9468A86D17958E.description: Explain that a stronger heart muscle can pump more blood with each beat.

F6A44860DFE301318D8E68A86D17958E.description: Describe and record the changes in heart rate before, during, and after physical activity.

F6A3F450DFE301318D8D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between the heart, lungs, muscles, blood, and oxygen during physical activity.

F6A361C0DFE301318D8B68A86D17958E.description: Discuss the need for oxygen and fuel to be available during ongoing muscle contraction so that heat and waste products are removed.

F6A31E80DFE301318D8A68A86D17958E.description: Explain that fluid needs are linked to energy expenditure.

F6A2DDC0DFE301318D8968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the body will adapt to increased workloads.

F6A29AF0DFE301318D8868A86D17958E.description: Explain the purpose of warming up before physical activity and cooling down after physical activity.

F6A24940DFE301318D8768A86D17958E.description: List and define the components of physical fitness.

F6A1F8C0DFE301318D8668A86D17958E.description: Identify the body's normal reactions to moderate to vigorous physical activity.

F6A156A0DFE301318D8468A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate knowledge of physical fitness concepts, principles, and strategies to improve health and performance.

F6A11600DFE301318D8368A86D17958E.description: Measure and record improvement in individual fitness activities.

F6A09200DFE301318D8168A86D17958E.description: Sustain continuous movement for increasing periods of time while participating in moderate to vigorous physical activity.

F69FFCE0DFE301318D7F68A86D17958E.description: Hold for an increasing period of time basic stretches for hips, shoulders, hamstrings, quadriceps, triceps, biceps, back, and neck.

F69F7350DFE301318D7D68A86D17958E.description: Climb a vertical pole or rope.

F69F2790DFE301318D7C68A86D17958E.description: Perform increasing numbers of each: abdominal curl-ups, oblique curl-ups on each side, modified push-ups or traditional push-ups with hands on a bench, forward lunges, side lunges, and triceps push-ups from a chair.

F69E7120DFE301318D7A68A86D17958E.description: Participate three to four days each week, for increasing periods of time, in continuous moderate to vigorous physical activities that require sustained movement of the large-muscle groups to increase breathing and heart rate.

F69DE660DFE301318D7868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to lift and carry objects correctly.

F69D2460DFE301318D7568A86D17958E.description: Students assess and maintain a level of physical fitness to improve health and performance.

F69CE050DFE301318D7468A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast folk dances, line dances, and circle dances.

F69C97A0DFE301318D7368A86D17958E.description: Define the terms folk dance, line dance, and circle dance.

F69C0710DFE301318D7168A86D17958E.description: Identify the differences between dribbling a ball (with the hand and the foot, separately) while moving forward and when changing direction.

F69BC3B0DFE301318D7068A86D17958E.description: Identify the key elements for increasing accuracy in rolling a ball and throwing a ball.

F69B7BB0DFE301318D6F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between throwing to a stationary partner and throwing to a moving partner.

F69B33F0DFE301318D6E68A86D17958E.description: Explain and demonstrate the correct hand position when catching a ball above the head, below the waist, near the middle of the body, and away from the body.

F69A8770DFE301318D6C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how changing speed and changing direction can allow one person to move away from another.

F699DD90DFE301318D6A68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate knowledge of movement concepts, principles, and strategies that apply to the learning and performance of physical activities.

F69994F0DFE301318D6968A86D17958E.description: Perform a line dance, a circle dance, and a folk dance with a partner.

F697B9D0DFE301318D6368A86D17958E.description: Foot-dribble a ball continuously while traveling and changing direction.

F6977620DFE301318D6268A86D17958E.description: Hand-dribble a ball continuously while moving around obstacles.

F6973200DFE301318D6168A86D17958E.description: Strike a ball continuously upward, using a paddle or racket.

F696E740DFE301318D6068A86D17958E.description: Kick a ball to a stationary partner, using the inside of the foot.

F696A190DFE301318D5F68A86D17958E.description: Throw and catch an object with a partner, increasing the distance from the partner and maintaining an accurate throw that can be easily caught.

F698CDB0DFE301318D6768A86D17958E.description: Throw a ball, using the overhand movement pattern with increasing accuracy.

F6988A40DFE301318D6668A86D17958E.description: Roll a ball for accuracy toward a target.

F6984640DFE301318D6568A86D17958E.description: Catch, while traveling, an object thrown by a stationary partner.

F69802C0DFE301318D6468A86D17958E.description: Balance while traveling and manipulating an object on a ground-level balance beam.

F6961A20DFE301318D5D68A86D17958E.description: Jump continuously a forward-turning rope and a backward-turning rope.

F694D230DFE301318D5968A86D17958E.description: Perform an inverted balance (tripod) by evenly distributing weight on body parts.

F6944FB0DFE301318D5768A86D17958E.description: Chase, flee, and move away from others in a constantly changing environment.

F693B600DFE301318D5568A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate the motor skills and movement patterns needed to perform a variety of physical activities.

document.title: Health Education Content Standards for California Public Schools, Kindergarten Through Grade Twelve

F9A91490DFE3013192BD68A86D17958E.description: Object appropriately to teasing or bullying of peers that is based on personal characteristics and perceived sexual orientation.

F9A8CFF0DFE3013192BC68A86D17958E.description: Encourage a school environment that is respectful of individual differences.

comments: Personal, family, and community health are interdependent and mutually supporting. The ability to promote the health of oneself and others reflects a well-rounded development and expression of health.
F9A88B00DFE3013192BB68A86D17958E.description: Health Promotion - All students will demonstrate the ability to promote and support personal, family, and community health.

F9A84760DFE3013192BA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to use self-control when angry.

F9A80250DFE3013192B968A86D17958E.description: Practice appropriate ways to respect and include others who are different from oneself.

F9A76F70DFE3013192B768A86D17958E.description: Carry out personal and social responsibilities appropriately.

F9A72670DFE3013192B668A86D17958E.description: Practicing Health-Enhancing Behaviors - All students will demonstrate the ability to practice behaviors that reduce risk and promote health.
comments: Practicing healthy behaviors builds competence and confidence to use learned skills in real-life situations. The ability to adopt health-enhancing behaviors demonstrates students' ability to use knowledge and skills to manage health and reduce risk-taking behaviors.

F9A6DCF0DFE3013192B568A86D17958E.description: Make a personal commitment to avoid persons, places, or activities that encourage violence or delinquency

F9A690A0DFE3013192B468A86D17958E.description: Describe how personal goals can be affected if violence is used to solve problems.

F9A64900DFE3013192B368A86D17958E.description: Make a plan to prevent and manage stress.

F9A60060DFE3013192B268A86D17958E.description: Goal Setting - All students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health.

document.title: California English Language Development Standards

571E29849EA340F98748A413ACF57D2D.description: Condense ideas in a variety of ways (e.g., through a variety of embedded clauses, or by compounding verb or prepositional phrases, nominalization) to create precise simple, compound, and complex sentences that condense concrete and abstract ideas (e.g., The epidemic, which ultimately affected hundreds of thousands of people, did not subside for another year).

840AACFC3F6347F6AC8E76F9A3634616.description: Condense ideas in a growing number of ways (e.g., through embedded clauses or by compounding verb or prepositional phrases) to create more precise and detailed simple, compound, and complex sentences (e.g., Species that could not adapt to the changing climate eventually disappeared).

F9B6BB369F6D466BA34CA17690EEA9FC.description: Condense ideas in a few basic ways (e.g., by compounding verb or prepositional phrases) to create precise and detailed simple, compound, and complex sentences (e.g., The students asked survey questions and recorded the responses).

D443DE668E7F4ECF9FEAA52B422E1325.description: Combine clauses in a variety of ways to create compound and complex sentences that make connections between and link concrete and abstract ideas, for example, to make a concession (e.g., While both characters strive for success, they each take different approaches to reach their goals), or to establish cause (e.g., Women's lives were changed forever after World War II as a result of joining the workforce).

4626B044192340569013C791345AB392.description: Combine clauses in a growing number of ways to create compound and complex sentences that make connections between and link concrete and abstract ideas, for example, to express a reason (e.g., He stayed at home on Sunday in order to study for Monday's exam) or to make a concession (e.g., She studied all night even though she wasn't feeling well).

16ECB8A66DD14A28A62CF5CD9B43F356.description: Combine clauses in a few basic ways (e.g., creating compound sentences using and, but, so; creating complex sentences using because) to make connections between and join ideas (e.g., I want to read this book because it tells the history of Pi).

22A6B67AB04B470D88AACD37AB86E018.description: Expand sentences with a variety of adverbials (e.g., adverbs, adverb phrases and clauses, prepositional phrases) to provide details (e.g., time, manner, place, cause) about a variety of familiar and new activities and processes.

AAD35905030440EDB8BA1D067572890E.description: Expand sentences with a growing variety of adverbials (e.g., adverbs, adverb phrases, prepositional phrases) to provide details (e.g., time, manner, place, cause) about familiar or new activities or processes.

378B33118B9749E78C2C9A342ED532E4.description: Expand sentences with simple adverbials (e.g., adverbs, adverb phrases, prepositional phrases) to provide details (e.g., time, manner, place, cause) about familiar activities or processes.

6F27955E651C4ACD8BD24BA5395D6613.description: Expand noun phrases in a variety of ways (e.g., complex clause embedding) to create detailed sentences that accurately describe concrete and abstract ideas, explain procedures and sequences, summarize texts and ideas, and present and critique points of view on a variety of academic topics.

5679E1C55A0A45B8A0ABD39478D5F77B.description: Expand noun phrases in a growing number of ways (e.g., adding adjectives to nouns, simple clause embedding) to create detailed sentences that accurately describe, explain, and summarize information and ideas on a variety of personal and academic topics.

3185F3E5354443FBB01B4E78EA56E6E2.description: Expand noun phrases to create increasingly detailed sentences (e.g., adding adjectives for precision) about personal and familiar academic topics.

44D3F5F22A7B450A893337D29B28B8D4.description: Use a variety of verbs in different tenses (e.g., past, present, future, simple, progressive, perfect), and mood (e.g., subjunctive) appropriate to the text type and discipline to create a variety of texts that describe concrete and abstract ideas, explain procedures and sequences, summarize texts and ideas, and present and critique points of view.

94B591EDA4DE496E85BC8CA3C3A6FC7A.description: Use a variety of verbs in different tenses (e.g., past, present, future, simple, progressive, perfect) appropriate to the text type and discipline to create a variety of texts that explain, describe, and summarize concrete and abstract thoughts and ideas.

B4F172FE72434FFA97F1B88F847CF16A.description: Use a variety of verbs in different tenses (e.g., past, present, future, simple, progressive) appropriate to the text type and discipline to create short texts on familiar academic topics.

4ABEA66F34084511AD94CC55056CCB13.description: Apply knowledge of familiar language resources for linking ideas, events, or reasons throughout a text (e.g., using connecting/transition words and phrases, such as on the contrary, in addition, moreover) to comprehending grade-level texts and writing cohesive texts for specific purposes and audiences.

F5F8AFA8A40F478588C0AE68482E60DD.description: Apply knowledge of a variety of resources for referring to make texts more cohesive (e.g., using nominalization, paraphrases, or summaries to reference or recap an idea or explanation provided earlier) to comprehending grade-level texts and to writing clear and cohesive texts for specific purposes and audiences.

3867B44372BC404CA314A339119E8C7B.description: Apply knowledge of familiar language resources for linking ideas, events, or reasons throughout a text (e.g., using connecting/transition words and phrases, such as meanwhile, however, on the other hand) to comprehending texts and to writing increasingly cohesive texts for specific purposes and audiences.

DEC7CF973D154A42878F7EE1C90BD7E0.description: Explain how successfully writers and speakers structure texts and use language (e.g., specific word or phrasing choices) to persuade the reader (e.g., by providing well-worded evidence to support claims or connecting points in an argument in specific ways) or create other specific effects, with light support.

DC7DE31B8CCD47BAA2563EC791DE8F0D.description: Explain how successfully writers and speakers structure texts and use language (e.g., specific word or phrasing choices) to persuade the reader (e.g., by providing well-worded evidence to support claims or connecting points in an argument in specific ways) or create other specific effects, with moderate support.

54C8CB04634D49D7837705A647AD1576.description: Explain how successfully writers and speakers structure texts and use language (e.g., specific word or phrasing choices) to persuade the reader (e.g., by providing evidence to support claims or connecting points in an argument) or create other specific effects.

AEFD3F13A8E14129974A8CD2F875133E.description: Evaluating how well writers and speakers use language to support ideas and arguments with details or evidence depending on modality, text type, purpose, audience, topic, and content area

36D7A9E2E3A146BC8F74EB92EAB781E2.description: Use knowledge of morphology (e.g., derivational suffixes), context, reference materials, and visual cues to determine the meaning, including figurative and connotative meanings, of unknown and multiple-meaning words on a variety of new topics.

C36A766789BF4419B47713FEA8AD38CF.description: Explain inferences and conclusions drawn from close reading of grade-level texts and viewing of multimedia using a variety of verbs and adverbials (e.g., creates the impression that, consequently).

00B02E9A37744587998F4DBA6117B053.description: Explain ideas, phenomena, processes, and relationships within and across texts (e.g., compare/contrast, cause/effect, themes, evidence-based argument) based on close reading of a variety of grade-level texts, presented in various print and multimedia formats, using a variety of detailed sentences and precise general academic and domain-specific words.

5D7EA5F09724473489F0EA6348DCDDBD.description: Explain inferences and conclusions drawn from close reading of grade-appropriate texts and viewing of multimedia using a variety of verbs and adverbials (e.g., indicates that, suggests, as a result).

D87B231455EB47EC9A5F28C35E31E75A.description: Explain ideas, phenomena, processes, and relationships within and across texts (e.g., compare/contrast, cause/effect, themes, evidence-based argument) based on close reading of a variety of grade-appropriate texts, presented in various print and multimedia formats, using increasingly detailed sentences, and a range of general academic and domain-specific words.

2B238CBBC38E4F5D91B03EB43DCAF5BD.description: Use knowledge of morphology (e.g., common prefixes and suffixes), context, reference materials, and visual cues to determine the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words on familiar topics.

53CD05285615400EAD5F59B2E76F0D59.description: Explain inferences and conclusions drawn from close reading of grade-appropriate texts and viewing of multimedia, using familiar verbs (e.g., seems that).

88DC9B5F14674B978FF57F096E3A1614.description: Explain ideas, phenomena, processes, and text relationships (e.g., compare/contrast, cause/effect, evidence-based argument) based on close reading of a variety of grade-appropriate texts, presented in various print and multimedia formats, using phrases, short sentences, and a select set of general academic and domain-specific words.

2D6584BD7C1547A5B8C3D8577C66A44C.description: Reading closely literary and informational texts and viewing multimedia to determine how meaning is conveyed explicitly and implicitly through language

78B5C931E2F04B40AB019066B9792F99.description: Demonstrate comprehension of oral presentations and discussions on a variety of social and academic topics by asking and answering detailed and complex questions that show thoughtful consideration of the ideas or arguments with light support.

3F19A4516F7A40C4B861716CDEB9D12A.description: Demonstrate comprehension of oral presentations and discussions on a variety of social and academic topics by asking and answering questions that show thoughtful consideration of the ideas or arguments with moderate support.

E2929144876646E1A00DBF9983144980.description: Demonstrate comprehension of oral presentations and discussions on familiar social and academic topics by asking and answering questions with prompting and substantial support.

1A437944B7954C1AB5C39F4CAEB13A1E.description: Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts

F5BFBA81D0F74B2F9BE0D8194E338D13.description: Interpretive (comprehension and analysis of written and spoken texts)

BA002188D9EE4A508C628DCC42959A89.description: Adjust language choices according to the task (e.g., group presentation of research project), context (e.g., classroom, community), purpose (e.g., to persuade, to provide arguments or counterarguments), and audience (e.g., peers, teachers, college recruiter).

35906C36EB3545F2928BACBABCD4C14D.description: Adjust language choices according to the context (e.g., classroom, community), purpose (e.g., to persuade, to provide arguments or counterarguments), task, and audience (e.g., peers, teachers, guest lecturer).

1C30379C01D84CE6A447292E1539B887.description: Adjust language choices according to the context (e.g., classroom, community) and audience (e.g., peers, teachers).

076AF7D981384757B7EA9639AD3FD8BA.description: Adapting language choices to various contexts (based on task, purpose, audience, and text type)

B7FB7C0504C242508F5258AA064A2AEC.description: Negotiate with or persuade others in discussions and conversations in appropriate registers (e.g., to acknowledge new information and politely offer a counterpoint) using a variety of learned phrases (e.g., You postulate that X. However, I've reached a different conclusion on this issue) and open responses to express and defend nuanced opinions.
