document.title: California Standards for Career Ready Practice

4F546495AD854ECC923AA45136FD4D32.description: Understand the environmental, social, and economic impacts of decisions.
comments: Career-ready individuals understand the interrelated nature of their actions and regularly make decisions that positively impact other people, organizations, the workplace, and the environment. They are aware of and utilize new technologies, understandings, procedures, and materials and adhere to regulations affecting the nature of their work. They are cognizant of impacts on the social condition, environment, workplace, and profitability of the organization.

948AB0BF500F49DA95053605367B8543.description: Employ valid and reliable research strategies.
comments: Career-ready individuals employ research practices to plan and carry out investigations, create solutions, and keep abreast of the most current findings related to workplace environments and practices. They use a reliable research process to search for new information and confirm the validity of sources when considering the use and adoption of external information or practices.

Career-ready individuals recommend ideas that solve problems in new and different ways and contribute to the improvement of the organization. They consider unconventional ideas and suggestions by others as solutions to issues, tasks, or problems. They discern which ideas and suggestions may have the greatest value. They seek new methods, practices, and ideas from a variety of sources and apply those ideas to their own workplace practices.

F603B17D90984C94B71EBD0C10FD2B6B.description: Work productively in teams while integrating cultural and global competence.
comments: Career-ready individuals contribute positively to every team, as both team leaders and team members. To avoid barriers to productive and positive interaction, they apply an awareness of cultural differences. They interact effectively and sensitively with all members of the team and find ways to increase the engagement and contribution of other members.

05313564F23B4D38872FE1396A070718.description: Model integrity, ethical leadership, and effective management.
comments: Career-ready individuals consistently act in ways that align with personal and community-held ideals and principles. They employ ethical behaviors and actions that positively influence others. They have a clear understanding of integrity and act on this understanding in every decision. They use a variety of means to positively impact the direction and actions of a team or organization, and they recognize the short-term and long-term effects that management's actions and attitudes can have on productivity, morale, and organizational culture.

B2E86A694BC04F10A403C7F324A36968.description: Act as a responsible citizen in the workplace and the community.
comments: Career-ready individuals understand the obligations and responsibilities of being a member of a community and demonstrate this understanding every day through their interactions with others. They are aware of the impacts of their decisions on others and the environment around them, and they think about the short-term and long-term consequences of their actions. They are reliable and consistent in going beyond minimum expectations and in participating in activities that serve the greater good.

BCA829EB214440D5A4D5F9FD2D78330D.description: Practice personal health and understand financial literacy.
comments: Career-ready individuals understand the relationship between personal health and workplace performance. They contribute to their personal well-being through a healthy diet, regular exercise, and mental health activities. Career-ready individuals also understand that financial literacy leads to a secure future that enables career success.

9D369ED732E44D69BF176C7B1A1F0F78.description: Utilize critical thinking to make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Career-ready individuals recognize problems in the workplace, understand the nature of the problems, and devise effective plans to solve the problems. They thoughtfully investigate the root cause of a problem prior to introducing solutions. They carefully consider options to solve a problem and, once agreed upon, follow through to ensure the problem is resolved.

Career-ready individuals find and maximize the productive value of existing and new technology to accomplish workplace tasks and solve workplace problems. They are flexible and adaptive in acquiring and using new technology. They understand the inherent risks—personal and organizational—of technology applications, and they take actions to prevent or mitigate these risks.

9C666BDA7FFD4A52973E014407BE6604.description: Develop an education and career plan aligned with personal goals.
comments: Career-ready individuals take personal ownership of their educational and career goals and manage their individual plan to attain these goals. They recognize the value of each step in the educational and experiential process, and they understand that nearly all career paths require ongoing education and experience to adapt to practices, procedures, and expectations of an ever-changing work environment. They seek counselors, mentors, and other experts to assist in the planning and execution of education and career plans.

F8864DA903B24E81995F32651D5E502D.description: Communicate clearly, effectively, and with reason.
comments: Career-ready individuals communicate thoughts, ideas, and action plans with clarity, using written, verbal, electronic, and/or visual methods. They are skilled at interacting with others: they are active listeners who speak clearly and with purpose, and they are comfortable with terminology that is common to workplace environments. Career-ready individuals consider the audience for their communication and prepare accordingly to ensure the desired outcome.

685611448402446983741EA0B5A5A8ED.description: Apply appropriate technical skills and academic knowledge.
comments: Career-ready individuals readily access and use the knowledge and skills acquired through experience and education. They make connections between abstract concepts with real-world applications and recognize the value of academic preparation for solving problems, communicating with others, calculating measures, and performing other work-related practices.

B7508976CCF84F1A8D2866402321A876.description: Explain a models limitations, misconceptions, and errors as applicable

B451BCAA2BFF41E580C05D6867B9B170.description: Safely plan and carry out investigations

61C46BAF3A9D41EF88C16C324FD1CE51.description: Introducing Scientific thinking, Modeling and Investigation Practices.

document.title: State of California Student Leadership Standards

85498DF7ADA142DCA5C548B52EDF1090.description:
The student leader acknowledges that images/video of students and staff should never be
presented in such a way that would embarrass or humiliate.

06E6FEE399F24674A57C6B08A32A9D9E.description:
The student leader demonstrates an understanding of the law and school/district policy
regarding the public sharing of images/video of minors on social media and in other public
forums, and works with school administration to protect student privacy.

32D08A8DBCCF4AD59D3A614C2C1AFDC5.description:
The student leader includes a diverse cross-section of the student body when creating video
or photo presentations to be shared school-wide.

F37F7E8D5B8C4D66AC455D8F17E0F5FE.description:
The student leader demonstrates a basic understanding of video and photography skills as
they relate to their role on the student leadership team.

F73E604049424478A52AFA99232BA3DA.description:
The student leader recognizes the role of video and photography in the promotion of positive
school culture.

203A70D2507242F0AFA5F39504D61034.description:
Video and Photography: As access to technology grows, student leaders are increasingly using visual/media arts to
promote a positive culture and climate at their schools. These tools have the power to connect
students to their school, but care must be taken to use these tools responsibly, and in a way
that is always positive and inclusive.

270F3792E110499E90BED747BBA74E7A.description:
The student leader demonstrates an understanding of the basic setup of an audio/visual
presentation and can connect a video source to both an audio and a video projection system.

3134ACE5B9BF4CE9AE20FA40EE07CD75.description:
The student leader selects music and other media that are appropriate for the nature of the
event, as well as to the values of the school community and the audience present at the event.

126560E1D7224B1B9E29167C882931B9.description:
The student leader demonstrates an understanding of the basic functions of a sound system
and can set up music and a microphone for any occasion.

966A38D7BAC046859384A4192C8A8A01.description:
The student leader creates an inclusive audio/visual environment that is accessible to all
audience members.

F5CD95924F0948469004133703ECE0F5.description:
The student leader recognizes the positive role of audio/visual technology in the creation of
school events.

9E997F2309054819A31FB5CC97A32268.description:
Audio/Visual Presentation: Student leaders are frequently called upon to not only use video and amplified sound in rallies,
assemblies, and outdoor activities, but also to set up the technology needed for these events as
well. The student leader should have the basic skills to set up this technology, as well as know
how to get the right music started to set the tone for the event.

4CD39BE5E92D4949BC1C982D28590E88.description:
The student leader manages personal data to maintain digital privacy and security for
themselves and for others.

F30E1B6C64BA497FA2411A1502D1993A.description:
The student leader demonstrates an understanding of and respect for the rights and
obligations of using and sharing intellectual property.

C698F42118754C919A5C2ECFD2EA83E4.description:
The student leader engages in positive, safe, legal, and ethical behavior when using
technology, including social interactions online or when using networked devices.

883A4D56F31B4BF7A2EE7188F6941A04.description:
The student leader cultivates and manages their digital identity and reputation, and
demonstrates awareness of the permanence of their actions in the digital world.

E9A882BF8EA14349998A14FA34313076.description:
Digital Citizenship: Whether on a shared classroom computer, at home, or on a mobile device, student leaders
have the power to connect to each other and to the world in ways that we never did at their
age. With this power comes the responsibility to understand their own digital footprint, as well
as to treat others with kindness, dignity, and respect.

5F5C7643BD67437B8DEA76B32DD893A0.description:
The student leader grants view, comment, and/or edit access to files as needed to allow for
collaboration with the student leadership team.

70713A8EAD354D418E309504CA63CA6E.description:
The student leader stores work in a shared cloud environment that is accessible by
themselves, their leadership team peers, and leadership team educators.

9B5221DAE2F641DFB1BC0C8B85F92B9F.description:
The student leader demonstrates a working knowledge of word processing, spreadsheets,
presentations, online forms, and desktop publishing as it relates to their role on the leadership
team.

6C98FC138E9B4C1E9A5F9496F1FBBD36.description:
Digital Workspace and Collaboration: It seems as though cloud technology was made for student leaders. The ability to collaborate
on budgets, scripts, to-do lists, calendars, and surveys, just to name a few, helps student
leaders to focus less on the back-and-forth of comparing different versions of documents, and
more on producing a better digital product to serve the student body. Comments, version
tracking, editing/suggesting mode, in-document chat, and other features enhance the student
leaders’ ability to communicate and collaborate whether in the same room, on a home
computer, or on their mobile device.

05021235BD6E4A619DD95DB25B02B028.description:
The student leader follows federal and state laws and district policy related to food and
beverage sales that take place during the school day.

4C09A0B5B62949E3BDF672A6641C7C53.description:
The student leader researches and tracks legislative bills and legal proceedings/judgements
that may influence student body activities, participation, procedures/codes, fundraising, or
accounting.

8E8FF1DF84C8437CAA9B52F22101D013.description:
The student leader adheres to federal, state, and local tax codes as they relate to student
body funds, funding, sponsorship, and re-sale permits.

A1BCCB0F10E44DD493E4D9C0C3B08813.description:
Business Law: In California and across the country, nutrition laws and accounting best practices have changed
dramatically in the last twenty years. Due to increased accountability and more rigorous
oversight, the student leader learns quickly that you can’t simply sell chocolate bars on campus
or nachos and soda at lunch to raise money. Awareness of business law, specifically as it
relates to nutrition and student body fund accounting, means that student leaders have a
greater awareness of how they can properly raise funds while preserving their California
non-profit status and complying with school, district, and state laws and policies.

AD05E1D4FDCF471798636F92B19C1D59.description:
The student leader attends to the needs of others in a positive manner in recognizing their
role as a representative of the entire student body, school, and community.

6149D88F4B6446BFA3A99D105720F2ED.description:
The student leader tracks and archives event participation data to identify trends in event
effectiveness and student engagement.

3242A5138E984F90BC4E93087D9692EB.description:
The student leader develops and implements crowd management and event safety plans
that include a mixture of structural (gates and barriers) and articulated (signage and
announcements) strategies.

B5EF8AE651494EB4A7CEC181A49AB9AD.description:
The student leader communicates with the public regarding current sales and offerings, and
develops a forum for customer feedback.

0669C0116B214C999A6C034C970CEFFD.description: The student leader exhibits positive customer interaction skills.

D6D72098A48D4E57ADF59E73D367FC56.description:
The student leader demonstrates the skills and competencies necessary to recognize
customer concerns and act to reach a satisfactory solution.

0DBD7BFFE1CF49E7A44AC4129970374A.description:
Customer Service: Student leaders are in sales. They sell tickets to dances and athletic events, fundraiser items,
spirit wear and student store items. They also “sell” free items--attendance at assemblies and
rallies, attendance at lunchtime activities, and in general the more abstract concepts of school
spirit and school involvement. Understanding who their clients are, what they want, and how
the expect to be treated helps the student leader to not only create products and experiences
that will better engage their customers in the short term, but will give them sales and customer
service experience they can carry with them into a future career.

4CDA2AD6919E4925B4CB94A75694CF1C.description:
The student leader experiments with different displays/product placement to produce
optimal interest and results.

6E0456326D5C442698AB2ABA7CD13C72.description: The student leader demonstrates creative ways to advertise.

E911A385776649E59179A12F10FAAEAA.description:
The student leader utilizes a variety of techniques and media to deliver the message to the
target audience.

138762C29A5D4A10B1F645F63844AFE5.description:
The student leader creates advertisements that are grammatically correct and visually
appealing.

3436208EB55E4A7694B3B7FFB6D4CDC3.description:
The student leader makes sure each advertisement contains all necessary information for
the product or event.

85943C51A78B4B188F5328DA46046457.description: The student leader identifies a target audience for each advertisement.

A092CC3528E84ECCB0FED42983D9A52E.description:
Advertising: Advertising is one part of your marketing strategy, specifically designed to sell or promote a
product or activity. Modern advertising blends the more traditional media of posters and flyers
with video production, photography, and social media. An effective advertising begins with
accurate and well-articulated information and comes to life with creativity and sensory appeal.

73C9C70083A94B68A90311A7D21A8620.description:
The student leader systematically develops and implements a marketing plan to deliver the
brand and/or marketing message to the target audience.

BB003B34E4894E7F96DDE807B6481307.description:
The student leader works collaboratively with the student leadership team to create a brand
and/or marketing message for the student leadership team, the student body, the school,
and/or school events.

2B3B4E43FBD34BC8A808B9568DB3475A.description: The student leader recognizes the difference between marketing and advertising.

C1758783855049A792A3FA8AC8210459.description:
Marketing: Marketing is a broad strategy. It involves the creation and nurturing of a brand and brand
message that connects the producer (student leaders) to their consumers. The American
Marketing Association defines it as “the activity, set of institutions, and processes for creating,
communicating, delivering, and exchanging offerings that have value for customers, clients,
partners, and society at large.”

E6050C94C56C4D108348C1EF999F4DC6.description:
The student leader evaluates each fundraising activity’s effectiveness for profitability and
efficient use of human and site resources.

2084B7F318294CC58AFD18B59E9A20D4.description:
The student leader serves as both a participant and leader in various fundraising activities
and employs effective sales techniques.

AD8819CCD7A842A791B02B0DF800E3C3.description:
The student leader orders merchandise and coordinates merchandise design and logistics
with vendors.

3E079ACA1BA74D30B42856E99DB55800.description:
The student leader projects income and expenses within a comprehensive pre-fundraiser
evaluation.

D6575CD738994D088E74A32BA7AC298C.description:
The student leader performs market research and identifies trends in student purchasing
preferences when selecting products and vendors for fundraising purposes.

AA4101E552284D28B2C9841445E7F080.description:
The student leader adheres to relevant laws, school board policies, and fiscal accountability
guidelines when selecting appropriate fundraising activities (i.e. state food guidelines,
recommended list of allowable-risk activities, etc.)

E76941AD02554DFF8F72028E94F2844D.description:
Fundraising: Building a successful leadership and activities program requires resources. While the LCAP and
LCFF have unlocked new discretionary resources for site administrators to use in promoting a
more positive school culture, the funding for these programs most often falls to a school’s
associated student body. Student leaders who learn effective fundraising practices and
techniques not only help bring in this much-needed revenue, but learn skills they can use in
college, career, and beyond.

A8FED901B90F4045B8010419B4C3B340.description:
The student leader identifies the various sources of school and student funding, the laws
and policies that dictate their allocation, and the structures/channels available for student input
and advocacy.

64823B44844A4EA8AABF6F9C862388FF.description:
The student leader consults the student body on budgetary decisions through the
representative process, public meeting, and open fiscal accountability, and spends student
body funds for the betterment of the student body.

D9DF6C55DBFB4BCD8D44072B008D9354.description: The student leader maintains accurate and accessible financial documents.

80064336D84A45E489297D63D1E142C1.description:
The student leader follows student body accounting procedures when performing
bookkeeping tasks, making purchases, receiving and disbursing funds, and reimbursing
vendors.

B0E125B7EA52459AA7302DD6877646D5.description: The student leader tracks income and expenses and identifies profit and loss.

66084140E84D4A46A7B6930CA0D7E28C.description:
The student leader evaluates past budgetary practices and collaborates on creating a
working budget for the current term.

83B47733CC20416E8234DE268B392619.description:
The student leader adheres to relevant laws, school board policy, and fiscal accountability
guidelines when managing the student body account.

343D3D894F7749AF80C77D2719554BA5.description:
Finance/Accounting: With a combination of school activities, athletics, and class activities, an associated student
body in California can easily have a six- or seven-digit figure annual budget to manage. School
staff (including administrators, athletic directors, leadership advisor, and account clerk or other
classified staff) often handle many of the day-to-day ASB transactions. However, students in
middle and high school ASBs are still considered by state law to be the stewards of all student
body funds. As such, student leaders should be involved at every level of student body fund
accounting, from the creation and approval of an budget, through the pre-approval and
disbursement of funds, and the collection of fundraiser monies, as well as the record-keeping of
all approvals through the ASB minutes.

1FBB1BFD62DD48C3AF133703CD437B02.description:
The student leader utilizes inclusive meeting strategies for brainstorming, prioritizing, and
project planning.

FB0A1D5FE55D40989F0FB66810C30B20.description: The student leader creates relevant agendas and maintains accurate minutes.

7460C64F7D9C41B79570890E4305CDB0.description: The student leader practices Parliamentary Procedure during formal business meetings.

9851F329E2C748CDA0E876CAD3D3A3D1.description: The student leader utilizes the principles of group dynamics in meeting protocols.

4AE88A95F93E408F91B342FCABE8F429.description:
Effective Meetings: The Business Meeting often serves as the backbone of the daily operation of student leadership
organizations. The adult advisor, the president, the secretary, and each individual member all
have a role to play in a productive meeting. By understanding the format and structure of an
effective meeting, student leaders can give all stakeholders a voice and more quickly get to the
planning and implementation of the programs and activities that create a positive school
culture.

79F602463CD74C2FB6209B5E2BECF71B.description:
The student leader chosen to participate on a selection committee shall practice fairness,
impartiality, open-mindedness, and confidentiality during and after the selection process.

3A35F1F956F7471680DDA3D79B075B31.description:
The student leader constructs a campaign speech or presentation and/or participates in an
interview process.

1AE6CF422EA643F7AD32B128F948D822.description: The student leader practices positive marketing and campaigning.

FF64A6212FC742A98C29479A8F0FD764.description:
The student leader campaigns and markets fairly in accordance with the school constitution
and bylaws.

3768927EC9D34E178F494022EF1896CA.description:
The student leader can articulate the purpose of a representative government and the
workings of a democracy.

35EE5C26E8384FF391D3D40B5DB3889F.description:
Elections and Appointments: When a student leader runs or applies for an elected or appointed office and wins, she wants to
know that she did so in a fair and equitable process. Likewise, the student who runs/applies
and does not get the job also wants to know that he lost fair and square. While the primary
responsibility for ensuring a fair and accessible election/selection process rests with the advisor
and administration, student leaders can contribute a great deal to the fairness and equality of
the process by following the rules and guidelines, encouraging their friends and supporters to
positively participate in the process, and then finally being a gracious winner or loser.

A8FB80CB2A964A7DA57312A829CA2C0D.description:
The student leader follows the established chain of command protocol for the student
leadership team, the school, and the school district.

58FB8DD5D80B4F9BB61B01F28286D155.description:
The student leader contributes to the creation of rules, regulations, agreements, and
contracts for student-led activities.

F1DF1B09919843BEB62AB2C8D64FD80F.description:
The student leader recognizes the ethical and legal implications of following or not following
established procedures, rules, regulations, agreements, and contracts.

1617BB4E0BC2483E8F80D8AE4460A322.description:
Procedures: Adherence to established policies and procedures is an important aspect of local, regional, and
national government. Teaching our students to identify and follow these formal and informal
protocols is an important part of their growth as entrusted leaders.

EC6C15C51C8C4829BF4FBE9C26130080.description:
The student leader acknowledges the right of students to form student clubs and
organizations in accordance with district, state, and federal guidelines.

EA10BCF2B9DF45B1B5664498644A75C5.description:
The student leader contributes to committees and/or councils and recognizes how the
committees and/or councils benefit the student leadership team.

F20694C1F763424F96E4562A97D8B6A2.description: The student leader reviews and/or creates a constitution and bylaws for the student body.

D0326FC40B154587A2D3D17F65420A76.description:
The student leader learns the chain of command that exists within their school and their
student body organization.

740209704EC946F1BCD97D2F86E574D6.description:
The student leader acknowledges the relationship of power and authority between the
student body organization, school staff, school district governing board, and state legislature.

4CC21CCBA5604FF394F9B0ABF8BA45D2.description:
The student leader identifies the purpose and function of government, the scope and limits
of authority, and the principle of “consent of the governed.”

CA3B2D2134C8452C930E73C49A59EDD5.description:
Authority and Governance: Student leadership offers our kids the opportunity to participate in the system of government
and procedures that exist on their campuses. It also allows them to make comparisons between
student government and local, state, and national government systems and policies, and to
experience the constraints within all government systems must operate.

5B48A884DAED487792A7A774FF218DDA.description:
The student leader demonstrates empathy for, and an awareness of social, cultural, and
societal norms for diverse locations and populations.

6AD73721B8284E0A9917A10867F1AB85.description: The student leader experiences and recognizes the benefit of serving others.

C1D7564792C34AED9A2DD04224C56641.description:
The student leader participates in a service activity or project to serve a specific need of
others.

475325A8DB1E4A799AA42A8C94754CC2.description:
The student leader establishes relationships with community leaders and community groups
to help address a community need.

11E54D70EF034F18884A932D1A9CCAAE.description:
Community Service: Serving others creates connections and awakens a sense of responsibility for societal
challenges. It also helps the leader identify needs within the community and fosters the
development of empathy and compassion.

37AE2E9BF7E24124A3A6BB40AFB5B8FA.description:
The student leader seeks both school and community feedback to evaluate and reflect upon
the impact of the project.

C17B30FCE6014B4FAA70AA080D59257F.description:
The student leader develops and implements a research-based plan of action to address a
specific community need.

A83FA45990DB4138947925F9F02915D5.description:
Utilizing academic skills, the student leader researches various solutions to a local need, and
integrates academic research into a service learning study.

1FB99D4CFA524044BA1588B2CBB277E2.description:
The student leader assesses the needs of the community by reaching out to community
leaders and local government.

F48266797CF94E2EA3E2F213DFB1144E.description:
The student leader recognizes the difference between service learning and community
service.

34C0C0E4E3684749B49B7300D31EDF92.description:
Service Learning Strategies: Informed global citizens need practical experiences -- at an early age, to effect change in their
communities and beyond. Fostering these opportunities (and follow up reflection) empowers
them to identify their responsibilities as members of the global community.

E26DFA15050847298CDD247CC1D0779D.description:
The student leader analyzes different forms of civic activism and ways in which citizens can
effect change in society.

B1AEBD92EA394D2781A7306C24F5DB54.description:
The student leader recognizes the value of membership in, and/or partnership with,
associations--groups of people organized for a joint purpose.

DCC484400C2E4B5C91F05D7FC0F71BBF.description: The student leader identifies the financial restrictions and guidelines of other organizations.

764FB8D1A54A42C4B3E796D5CF071C24.description:
The student leader develops partnerships with various student, school, parent, and
community groups.

C16AF6317E5F4159B445E6BFE829F6B8.description:
The student leader acknowledges differing backgrounds (cultural, religious, geographic,
special needs, socio-economic, gender identity, sexual orientation) and includes diverse
perspectives to promote an inclusive school culture.

1F242781E993439EA7E5152F46AAA48E.description:
The student leader identifies differing social and cultural norms and then raises awareness of
those norms to promote acceptance and inclusion.

AD481E49B5274BB08A9D6D309D3E9B3F.description: The student leader seeks and offers help when needed.

3BF591643F5A400C8D39913B386E89C8.description: The student leader negotiates conflict constructively.

C6EC8C54AC0C46B29247DA105A1AE0DE.description: The student leader resists inappropriate social pressure.

A396FBCD76B94517B1DBCAF4C36910BE.description:
The student leader establishes and maintains healthy relationships with the student
leadership team, the student body, and adults.

000A7DEBD1954462867B07F7E313D934.description:
The student leader makes informed decisions about behavior and social interactions that
consider the consequences of one’s actions and the well-being of oneself and others.

98696BDE503044D2A01B09EE0F5A565B.description:
The student leader will practice self-management by regulating thoughts, emotions, and
behaviors in various situations as they relate to stress, motivation, discipline, and impulse
control.

FF047E1FA2114547A210968BF9E3C7C5.description:
The student leader analyzes one’s strengths and areas of improvement to develop a
validated self-perception, self-competence, and growth mindset.

4282BDB9B75B459486D5C3C9D3679F25.description:
The student leader identifies emotions, thoughts, and values that impact behavior and self
efficacy.

4B87FF0EAF0342F2A43E84F85BFA17C3.description:
Social and Emotional Learning: A harmonious environment where all leaders feel validated, accepted, and important is
necessary to facilitate cooperation within the group. Individual leaders need to develop self
awareness and an appreciation for the diversity of others in order to utilize their strengths and
contribute positively to the group.

1D8A6ED9CAD44FCA864BA65ED5B29134.description: The student leader gives feedback to peers in a positive and constructive manner.

DB8F26F018B440A288C9FC4502121CEC.description:
The student leader self-evaluates, solicits peer and advisor feedback, and makes
adjustments to goals, behavior, and processes as necessary.

DA75ED2766CE4B43B8C75FB1B413DFEE.description:
The student leader creates timelines for meeting goals and monitors progress to ensure
on-time completion.

5D0F862F998A4492A2A76FA425888E96.description: The student leader creates a plan of action for achieving goals.

4ED43779F887468F889C19159F621D4D.description: The student leadership team sets attainable goals to improve school culture and climate.

35A372AB14F14D14AD3A53DFB90A0C12.description: The student leader sets short-term and long-term personal goals.

C0ACE5A0BDA7493D8D28FC11DCFF7F77.description:
Goal Setting, Feedback, and Evaluation: Identifying vision and a systematic plan for implementation of the team’s goals leads to its
ultimate success. The team should first identify why its mission is important and then set
attainable goals to achieve its objectives.

8B0C93ABEDD34D4AA496EA8F73BFB122.description: Once made, the student leader supports decisions of the group.

71B10E637E5E45A788199B594A1121B2.description:
The student leader considers diverse ideas, synthesizes viewpoints, and analyzes claims and
evidence on all sides of an issue when considering possible solutions.

A508A70EA8344A98B1A32443FD3BACB8.description:
The student leader recognizes and utilizes various models of decision-making (e.g.,
authoritative, consensus, democratic, individual)

04306137C6CF4CD58254F8B3CCC8FA84.description: The student leader delegates authority when appropriate.

DF3C733F98FF4A458EF91370286363B1.description: The student leader celebrates accomplishments and recognizes the contributions of others.

5AC230D29FB446DD8CFE37156A222E91.description: The student leader enlists others to share a common vision.

661D68B42E494A12AD210D85F4E9F915.description: The student leader serves as a participating member of a group.

74D3AF4524EA423F964F8CB6F0B2D5BB.description:
The student leader assumes a leadership role in an activity or group work that allows them to
facilitate and direct the group’s activities.

4014FB81E3654EA68DD3A3951D35068B.description:
The student leader appreciates the diversity of others, and the value of representing a
diverse student body.

841088CC05134037981773861D84A1B2.description:
The student leader acknowledges different personality types and how to work together in an
all-inclusive group setting.

66ED76DC08CE456F9204CD485DEF003D.description:
Group Dynamics: Effective leaders work collaboratively to create vision, purpose, and direction for their team.
Particular emphasis on positive group dynamics leads to the best possible outcome for the
team’s mission.

500A5417D90047019DA9CA639B203831.description:
The student leader acknowledges and celebrates the strengths and accomplishments of
others.

5134E7D859474F13A1BABD11E97AEA9C.description:
The student leader takes initiative by assessing where a need exists, and assisting without
being asked, when appropriate.

46156A51A6C740119B143E3FF15E1411.description:
The student leader utilizes a combination of traditional, non-traditional, and other creative
approaches to idea generation, activity planning, and problem solving.

024AEEA98A1446E7B4ECB1C42FA0CDFD.description:
The student leader practices problem solving skills, including identifying the problem,
soliciting possible solutions from members of the leadership team, and then implementing an
agreed-upon solution.

FAC75FCF4F254A5589A32C40CE572664.description: The student leader communicates feelings using “I” statements.

E01094D498E245E086E7A3F4373AC0B8.description: The student leader treats others with compassion and empathy.

FBF79F0F0F9F40658FF2602D003E4DE0.description:
The student leader articulates their own point of view and utilizes active listening to hear
others’ points of view to arrive at a mutual decision.

F2AA13E9968D45FC93C7CB50CC2D463B.description:
The student leader practices active listening skills, including positive facial expression, eye
contact, posture, summarizing, and eliminating distractions.

06794603903D40B4949512962BF09C51.description: The student leader understands the difference between passive and active listening.

7ABE8BB06FBE4A4888F370D272CBE160.description:
The student leader acknowledges the value of teamwork and consensus building in all
aspects of student leadership.

D525638AA2E34FEA868855D4FE06EB29.description:
Interpersonal Skills: Strong leaders possess exceptional interpersonal skills that focus on active listening, taking
initiative, and collaborating positively.

AF73EB3978994BF186FF066DC9517CAB.description:
The student leader seeks out evaluation and feedback from previous events to inform the
planning and implementation of future events.

EABE44DBC6604F19A7429850ACFAEE16.description:
Periodically, the student leader evaluates the job performance of their leadership peers to
provide both personal and organizational growth.

B4EFBF30112A4BF29956BCBF55CE52DC.description:
The student leader uses appropriate tone and language to provide constructive written and
oral feedback.

F04024B3FB6348FEBED27DFBF072DC25.description:
Following an activity, the student leader reflects upon the activity’s successes and areas for
growth through an individual, small group, whole group, and/or whole school evaluation
process.

C485B8B26B28473C9DB8E1C657808368.description:
The student leader acknowledges the value of feedback for both personal and organizational
growth.

129F9285B67D4A45BABA536211CC5A72.description:
Evaluation and Feedback: Effective leaders continually self evaluate and seek the feedback of outside observers in order
to expand their leadership skills.

490C0F793144481DA5B7BD4E8171A7FF.description:
The student leader considers diverse ideas, synthesizes viewpoints, and analyzes claims and
evidence on all sides of an issue when considering possible solutions.

E26246B0E5504176B331CB069162FBCA.description:
The student leader seeks out opportunities for the school community to share problems and
concerns.

E5A6C03EB1254FF38A2FB0D48E2C1CE8.description:
The student leader provides a forum for discussion surrounding problems that the school
population may be facing.

FEF97E5E167C4B8B94336D8BF69B5A16.description:
The student leader seeks out adult (advisor, counselor, administrator) intervention when
appropriate.

90A15CF3F486451F85483825366919E7.description:
In a group conflict, the student leader identifies individuals’ roles in the conflict, utilizes
active listening techniques with the group, acknowledges their own role in the conflict, and
reaches group consensus on a path forward.

D5CA70A2655F4B5C9F49BC9D203F06C8.description:
In an individual conflict, the student leader utilizes active listening techniques, acknowledges
their role in the conflict, and reaches mutual agreement on a path forward.

517472D5E7CA463797F70915AE61C1D8.description:
The student leader identifies the presence of a conflict and determines whether it is an
individual or group conflict.

63B03D2AB28D496C9F37D86D6CE463DE.description:
Conflict Resolution: Managing groups requires developing and refining skills related to listening, advising, effectively
communicating, and seeking outside support as needed.

F3ED2B752EDB4FA995F574020B8444A1.description: The student leader prepares location and manpower.

0F30DFA577DE4E2BB8753ECC9EB823CC.description: The student leader has the opportunity to try the process again and again.

CB3449FA4E514256A22842B2B7BC613F.description: The student leader plans ahead for potential problems.

FB21C0D7AA7E4D3F9944F3482068A04A.description: The student leader acknowledges when and who to talk to for questions and assistance.

CB698C99FB924F51A8D7A3744448DC82.description:
The student leader demonstrates knowledge of appropriate comments to encourage
cooperation.

2AB9B84C28E0401F8A85F57693B2695C.description: The student leader understands the importance of providing a safe location.

EA64F1D7E5D844E98FC3F1C79E952F5A.description:
Crowd Management: Effective group management requires good planning and an awareness of the location and
composition of the group.

CFFB74F99CB04924AB447615F6DB7A51.description:
The student leader effectively incorporates a variety of media and/or realia into speech
content when applicable.

436892BC40B74105A3736F192E8025FA.description:
The student leader demonstrates a variety of techniques to connect with the audience and to
maintain the audience’s attention.

D8EB04B3675647E3836A0454C78E4275.description: The student leader utilizes effective body language and eye contact.

5716AEB5ECF24B698AAEADFF4FDF68C9.description: The student leader uses appropriate volume, tone, emphasis, and diction.

E8DF2BF9F8CA46388FB7BE32FA7ABC74.description: The student leader utilizes standard microphone procedures.

8E4545C3C8384B4BABF88BA66C85A958.description: The student leader plans and executes accurate pace and timing.

6037E3FC63FB44A5AA0570B95FCB5EC8.description:
The student leader acknowledges the audience and purpose of the occasion and adapts
speech and content accordingly.

1E4E49D4EBD94BA0B9C9A848B4AA5C6B.description:
Public Speaking: Student leaders speak in the public arena in formal and informal settings. A variety of verbal and
non-verbal factors ensure the success of their communication.

510D6B1B9FB344C1A53D7BB35555DAF6.description:
The student leader actively listens and responds during the interview process to demonstrate
understanding.

A2F81B66A8AC4C4E846250E14C000F1E.description: The student leader prepares and asks valuable questions.

DB3FDDCEF80E4529AA4DD66BD4042887.description: The student leader exemplifies confidence and attentiveness.

D61CB2AC720C499F81D85BE75FD25B15.description: The student leader demonstrates appropriate and professional appearance.

75F9BDBD19EC4AADAC0A3A4ADD10BDDB.description:
The student leader anticipates possible interview questions and rehearses potential
responses.

50406B69C91841E68CAF32DBB7A650AE.description: The student leader identifies areas of personal strength and growth.

EC6F89B38F9E4100AC024D7C38EEA9CD.description:
The student leader researches and investigates the mission and vision of the organization, as
well as the desired position.

EF5CEC6D9F424039A267FFDFAC092F98.description:
Interviewing Skills: Student leaders encounter interviews in a variety of different settings. Appointed candidates are
interviewed for selection; experienced officers are sometimes called upon to reverse roles and
become the interviewer. By sitting on both sides of the table, student leaders can gain valuable
college and career interview skills.

273CE8A307CB47F399D19A2D94FFAA99.description: The student leader creates and sends personalized thank you notes.

5FF991BAB549457C9E5208453EF57C77.description: The student leader plans and organizes a meeting agenda using appropriate format.

CAB2D023B9DA41B6B5B48AEB1D1A4724.description: The student leader creates eye-catching, effective social media messages.

F0C0CE8804F4441CAFA6A99E8EBD9D55.description: The student leader creates eye-catching, effective posters and flyers.

04BDCEAC0C954E62BFD8DF04AF3D8781.description: The student leader creates an auto-dialer and/or telephone message script.

7D87B6BA12C04535B7D559BAE955A7D5.description: The student leader creates a press release.

72D269D899144EC0BA8CCE68FD0CBD4F.description: The student leader creates an invitation suitable for the occasion and audience.

BD4A1B82BC5B4A7A908A3E1B8B6E63B6.description: The student leader organizes, writes, and publishes attention-grabbing messages suitable for the occasion and audience.

0DB5B76E170044A39982BCF920EB50ED.description: The student leader creates a résumé and/or portfolio.

87F2227F251E4BC4BF8B7F87B3F0A3C0.description: The student leader uses appropriate tone and language when giving written feedback.

7D86E54865CC4C448250157E0DF1762E.description: The student leader prepares and presents committee reports.

0CB6BCD9E3B94F1A94DF3DE03677E999.description: The student leader applies knowledge of proper tone, formatting, and the appropriate use of business or friendly email.

86AB81E5CB064116AD0A4A63E07A8EB1.description: The student leader applies knowledge of proper tone, formatting, and the appropriate use of business or friendly letters.

18A8453B97A946F8B2DAD8BFE1D78C1B.description:
Written Communication: Written communication is the foundation of the student leadership program. Even when words
are meant to be spoken (e.g., Homecoming script, auto-dialer message to families), it all begins
with the written word.

of time.

34BEA02AFB294412BFF5682888F24E78.description:
Initiate or engage in simple physical
activities for a short to moderate
period of time.

288227DCCEA940F3B0792BAFCE9CD125.description:
Demonstrate more precision and
efficiency during two-handed fine
motor activities.

59DFAD3C47024B49817401455BCAC4C5.description:
Can place an object or own body
in front of, to the side, or behind
something else with greater
accuracy.

1D6DA244267242ADA30A6E892A1FEFE7.description:
Can change directions quickly
and accurately.

1BADE241FA574E70BB74024056988FD4.description:
Begin to understand and distinguish
between the sides of the body.

8C70508C9C504BF385280D966EA00F26.description: Use any two body parts together.

097BD3E7BCD54374A360CE572FFD61DC.description:
Can place an object on top of
or under something with some
accuracy.

3BBA3CDD4DA74D30BCB347EC53282D58.description:
Move forward and backward or up
and down easily.

E1AA617446C346EA8BFF8FA6BF0F7E7A.description:
Distinguish movements that are up
and down and to the side of the body
(for example, understands “use that
side, now the other side”).

4971D5D541B944348011B79000E446D2.description:
Use own body, general space, and
other people’s space when locating or
relating to other people or objects in
space.

6E81DBADECCD4D33AE3AEBD1777D7088.description:
Use own body as reference point
when locating or relating to other
people or objects in space.

ED265CE200D346CF97DDFB2E26B37B76.description:
Demonstrate knowledge of an
increasing number of body parts.

BF8C701650904E69A07C96D47CC61AC9.description:
Demonstrate knowledge of the names
of body parts.

E6E5F2BB190547C9AF694FB2D905FD93.description:
Show increasing fine motor manipulative skills using hands and arms such
as in-hand manipulation, writing,
cutting, and dressing.

28EA18935670499BAAA3006D7561F41C.description:
Show gross motor manipulative skills
by using arms, hands, and feet with
increased coordination, such as rolling a ball underhand, tossing underhand, bouncing, catching, striking,
throwing overhand, and kicking.

E70269592D4147749CD8A9530472FC15.description:
Begin to show fine motor manipulative skills using hands and arms such
as in-hand manipulation, writing,
cutting, and dressing.

257AA456AC27495F9DA62E51CBFCC248.description:
Begin to show gross motor manipu -
lative skills by using arms, hands, and
feet, such as rolling a ball underhand,
tossing underhand, bouncing, catching, striking, throwing overhand, and
kicking.

493DA4FA21D64A44B397CC5679819914.description:
Demonstrate increasing ability and
body coordination in a variety of
locomotor skills, such as galloping,
sliding, hopping, and leaping.

C3165C6C0BF449339158EB6E61774154.description:
Jump for height (up or down) and for
distance with increasing competence.
Uses arm swing to aid forward jump.

6AF762A4D9FA44C8A584335F8FB24032.description:
Run with a longer stride length and
each foot off the ground for a greater
length of time. Opposition of arms
and legs is more consistent.

23C1F221B85B4CC98AE94A98EA304547.description:
Walk with balance, oppositional arm
movements, and relatively narrow
base of support (space between feet).

065AE7442CE84B5DB69465F6BA44F8B4.description:
Begin to demonstrate a variety of
locomotor skills, such as galloping,
sliding, hopping, and leaping.

402B6C3BDE7D44EEBA35A7977D3B8A1C.description:
Jump for height (up or down) and for
distance with beginning competence.

D67589F26D824CAC970673B54AC5084B.description:
Run with short stride length and
feet off the ground for a short period
of time. May show inconsistent
opposition of arms and legs.

4EDEE06F66174FFCBCA24A773CEB237D.description:
Walk with balance, not always stable,
oppositional arm movements still
developing, and relatively wide base
of support (space between feet).

C308233F85AE4B1E965724ACF11D3BCD.description:
Show increasing balance control while
moving in different directions and
when transitioning from one movement or position to another.

088C66F2902C4E28BA186B80D7B4AD67.description:
Show increasing balance and control
when holding still.

17E19A620A4840B4B8AAC1BE467021E4.description:
Maintain balance while in motion
when moving from one position to
another or when changing directions,
though balance may not be completely stable.

E56605DAE1054244BFB6C7B82972FB7E.description:
Maintain balance while holding still;
sometimes may need assistance.

B0FD29D3D74C40879E9D7E8FAE2AE5B8.description:
Communicate and express feelings
intentionally through dance.

113BC5F153964AB1B7699F1B0AA62CDB.description:
Improvise more complex dances
that have a beginning, middle, and an
end.

7C00003641FC4BB48F7164FB22C1D7B6.description:
Extend understanding and skills for
acting out and dramatizing through
music and movement patterns.

EA28A5C75CD848B8A67C76C324C24EEB.description:
Communicate feelings spontaneously
through dance and begin to express
simple feelings intentionally through
dance when prompted by adults.

FF148C23AFAB4EFFB4D73B3D384BA2E2.description:
Improvise simple dances that have
a beginning and an end.

317060F9116B479EB0AF98AE5381AC4F.description:
Begin to act out and dramatize
through music and movement
patterns.

A6DAD79D11534D4F84382CADCF8A0842.description: Create, Invent, and Express Through Dance

384A38271BAB4CAFA45047A572FCC286.description:
Demonstrate some advanced skills
in responding to tempo and timing
through movement.

AFEF802C1BB946B1A097F546434AAFC2.description:
Show advanced awareness and
coordination of movement with other
people in dance or when moving
in space.

A953AB2E82A147CE958C9EB43F6B3E06.description:
Continue to develop awareness
of body in space.

089A6A773D6F41CBB09550B762334718.description:
Begin to respond to tempo and
timing through movement.

C0075BD3D7894B5BBEF8640C0F301EC0.description:
Begin to be aware of other people
in dance or when moving in space.

077E7AD9ACE9409ABD79193F1782C5A9.description:
Begin to be aware of own body
in space.

BC0CCF34EBF3412480468F50615ED62A.description:
Use understanding of different steps
and movements to create or form
a dance.

88FDA9ED5DBC44D69877BCC93DC10C54.description:
Respond to instruction of more than
one skill at a time in movement, such
as turning, leaping, and turning again.
Often initiate a sequence of skills.

CF22EE0E4E1841D7859A975BA6914AFA.description:
Connect dance terminology with
demonstrated steps.

AA8591A6F5214E398DAEB7F3C2A4F989.description:
Further engage and participate
in dance movements.

55E3BA6347D04DBFB407EAB49F42E334.description:
Explore and use different steps
and movements to create or form
a dance.

44A49B403D7149AF83C77A526A06DE34.description:
Respond to instruction of one skill
at a time during movement, such as
a jump or fall.

BF28F0C2276942D29C9CB45207269E1B.description:
Begin to understand and use
vocabulary related to dance.

68D26418A3C54F1EBA4341F1B35B4B6C.description:
Create and use an increasing variety
of props, costumes and scenery to
enhance dramatization of familiar
stories and fantasy play with peers.

408F1575BA54406B8D72DB7E91AFF4F3.description:
Demonstrate extended role-play skills
with increased imagination and
creativity.

E74DF86A9A564F4C9AF9160D23D77DD7.description:
Add props and costumes to enhance
dramatization of familiar stories and
fantasy play with peers.

4DD1E205B4F1498FA030AF844FD288E3.description:
Demonstrate basic role-play skills
with imagination and creativity.

1FEA8A1187FC4917B79DF383C5025C1D.description: Develop Skills to Create, Invent, and Express Through Drama

2661F5E1A0C649ADBCCAD23A72A2B1B0.description:
Demonstrate knowledge of extended
plot and conflict of a participatory
drama.

C483641C622649339A6974C4A71B5F96.description:
Explain preferences and interests
related to participating in drama.

8DF514E6EEDA4AD490CE162099D7DA71.description:
Demonstrate a broader understanding
of drama vocabulary.

37D9DB28B66C410DB97CB0F1A157A1BE.description:
Demonstrate knowledge of simple
plot of a participatory drama.

2056F710BAC84709BD28E22E9A83532C.description:
Identify preferences and interests
related to participating in drama.

A1982087CF1E4CA4A16F9A3502C5D805.description:
Demonstrate an understanding of
simple drama vocabulary.

6E6D9DA45FC74F4081E8F58E235D99DE.description:
Explore, improvise, and create brief
melodies with voice or instrument.

8AA023AA7E9E4504A1F4E737FC2A6FAA.description:
Move or use body to demonstrate
beat, tempo, and style of music,
often intentionally.

36C2530115D845A196B5E1A35F2A42CF.description:
Continue to apply vocal and instrumental skills and use instruments
to produce more complex rhythms,
tones, melodies, and songs.

2C1EC85F25C44D898FB4694F682383E5.description:
Move or use body to demonstrate
beat and tempo, often spontaneously.

CE93A96FF04943D0B1EFA3217FAD11E6.description:
Explore vocal and instrumental skills
and use instruments to produce
simple rhythms and tones.

D532D213592E4BCBA1D1E75AAD1BDC5E.description: Create, Invent, and Express Through Music

D07D6F887F3441338863AC3975C871E2.description:
Extend vocal exploration; sing
repetitive patterns and entire songs
alone and with others in wider
ranges of pitch.

AD3767A06CAB434BBE0C0788A5F77BC5.description:
Become more able to discriminate
between different voices and various instrumental and environmental
sounds. Follow words in a song.

C3D23C2279C84AA79BFEC4F8A1C82255.description:
Explore vocally; sing repetitive
patterns and parts of songs alone
and with others.

21093C648A26407D8AF92FD239F9607A.description:
Begin to discriminate between different voices and certain instrumental
and environmental sounds. Follow
words in a song.

576E47999D2A4E9F949498EA7BA60FBC.description:
Use body movement freely and
more accurately to respond to beat,
dynamics, and tempo of music.

D06C3BE337464A1C85434D7E0E1DE45E.description:
Identify the sources of a wider
variety of music and music-like
sounds.

CE14C55104FF4556B9A2A57C8023E4E7.description:
Demonstrate more complex repeating
melody and rhythm patterns.

192D95645E4843D7857F2E6DE5A4BBA5.description:
Verbally reflect on music and
describe music by using an
expanded vocabulary.

73F3960226A04DF199D9AED5443BE6CC.description:
Use body movement freely to respond
loosely to beat—loud versus quiet
(dynamics)—and tempo.

DF42FFF3D32A4D96B179AA12AE98484E.description:
Identify the sources of a limited
variety of musical sounds.

64C7FAC593BA40EF8851112C8270E964.description:
Recognize simple repeating melody
and rhythm patterns.

7546942F5C844BF98487C954F4AE5BBB.description:
Sustain attention and begin to reflect
verbally about music; demonstrate
familiarity with words that describe
music.

FE5A4F23565249A89D6509AD0DE4B1B2.description:
Use intensity of marks and color
more frequently to express a feeling
or mood.

91A83D0C59CA4CC7BEE5D17400964BB5.description:
Draw more detailed figures or
objects with more control of line
and shape.

E65FC52C91DF4B7D85730AB8229E9D4D.description:
Intentionally create content in a
work of art.

7981A218764A44C2AE57267C0A7E02A3.description:
Begin to use intensity of marks and
color to express a feeling or mood.

AC9781E2BCA74544B9182E03CB9101BC.description: Begin to draw figures or objects.

DA2AC668B4964F1985CCF5575E70D0CE.description:
Create art and sometimes name
the work.

BB02E17015D74B38A813A0290DFBC02E.description: Create, Invent, and Express Through Visual Art

663432E6B0624A979D4815BC8459C463.description:
Demonstrate increasing coordination
and motor control when working
with visual arts tools.

29C2D81A643A4A4889EC2A18D1AF6E1A.description:
Recognize and name materials
and tools used for visual arts.

3EC5772CF2CD4AC6A630EA9B63A2B451.description:
Use paper and other materials to
make two- and three-dimensional
assembled works.

5B2859E00AAB48138C8C3D2F690447D6.description:
Make more representational forms
out of dough or clay, using tools
(for example, a rolling pin or a garlic
press).

B9DB1D64EB724A33931675BCAE93F02F.description:
Begin to create representative paintings or drawings that approximate or
depict people, animals, and objects.

5D8F09FCBC2645B49BD2B5F292B2EB07.description:
Draw single circle and add lines
to create representations of people
and things.

092EE5DB55524A21883F4F52D530A4E1.description:
Demonstrate some motor control
when working with visual arts tools.

50B9138E53344BA88D06CF09389A330E.description:
Begin to recognize and name
materials and tools used for visual
arts.

373DF5C1851E4FA598CDE0A2447F74B8.description: Begin to use paper and other materials to assemble simple collages.

00EEC042A2B34AEC9952015E7599AD0A.description:
Make somewhat regular-shaped balls
and coils out of dough or clay.

AA0DD083A02040C1BCC48D9D2B8FEAA5.description:
Begin to create paintings or drawings
that suggest people, animals, and
objects.

86C73B7278F848308B3DDC64EE316F1D.description:
Make straight and curved marks
and lines; begin to draw rough circle
shapes.

78E583531A5B447AB491EC148DB67219.description:
Choose own art for display in the
classroom or for inclusion in a portfolio or book and explain her or his
ideas in some detail.

CB7D25A1205947BF942BB94E06DB5D1B.description:
Enjoy and engage with displays of
visual art. May expand critical assessment of visual art to include preferences for types of artwork or art
activities.

6CF53760C009499DAA1CC2D1971E1D19.description:
Begin to plan art and show increasing
care and persistence in completing it.

390531DEB0CE4454B9DA69AFF07490C6.description:
Communicate about elements
appearing in art (such as line, texture,
or perspective), and describe how
objects are positioned in the artwork.

34A6832AEA114FC99F21C5A6746B95D3.description:
Choose own art for display in the
classroom or for inclusion in a
portfolio or book and briefly
explain choice.

4CDC8B2710B146DC9B8955DB959FF1FE.description:
Enjoy and engage with displays of
visual art, inside or outside the classroom. Begin to express preferences
for some art activities or materials.

67EC465105174801BF43E2F8B7DB2BFE.description:
Create marks with crayons, paints,
and chalk and then identify them;
mold and build with dough and clay
and then identify them.

85DA8CCA70714A96AD18BE011DD1C895.description:
Notice and communicate about
objects or forms that appear in art.

document.title: California Preschool Learning Foundations Volume 3

80A61222C2914A9596F944695284EDD2.description:
Demonstrate an increased awareness and the ability to discuss in
simple terms how to care for the
environment, and participate in
activities related to its care.

472E25AD4BB04DFB9467C5CC42D404BF.description:
Demonstrate an increased ability to
notice and describe the effects of
weather and seasonal changes on
their own lives and on plants and
animals.

B47A65FD55DA490BA7EEF4D9D31BB730.description:
Demonstrate an increased ability
to observe, describe, and discuss
changes in weather.

0118DA7B8351453D850FBFA41BC51B18.description:
Demonstrate an increased ability to
observe and describe natural objects
in the sky and to notice patterns of
movement and apparent changes in
the sun and the moon.

DDFC2CA9DFBB4A1B8D6907E6C395233E.description:
Develop awareness of the
importance of caring for and
respecting the environment and
participate in activities related
to its care.

191D7D0DA9C74208A994CB1B366241FC.description:
Begin to notice the effects of
weather and seasonal changes
on their own lives and on plants
and animals.

99F686EEA6A84BD0883484C998C02578.description:
Notice and describe changes
in weather.

350E329882614843841574CE7CB4D94D.description:
Observe and describe natural objects
in the sky (sun, moon, stars, clouds)
and how they appear to move and
change.

6D4CAC12E8BE4C04AF3576C96BEE2500.description:
Demonstrate increased ability
to investigate and compare characteristics (size, weight, shape, color,
texture) of earth materials such as
sand, rocks, soil, water, and air.

6BB6B1A7C51947E19BA558DF79F9FAD9.description:
Investigate characteristics (size,
weight, shape, color, texture) of earth
materials such as sand, rocks, soil,
water, and air.

08FC576F65F9403889F7618147E65590.description: Properties and Characteristics of Earth Materials and Objects

48729F68B56844A597E0E7BF194EF466.description: Develop a greater understanding of the basic needs of humans, animals, and plants (e.g., food, water, sunshine, shelter).

D7A0FEC742EE48A1BDC48B08ED55EA56.description: Observe and explore growth in humans, animals, and plants and demonstrate an increased understanding that living things change as they grow and go through transformations related to the life cycle (for example, from a caterpillar to butterfly)

3107CF6EAD1F40B4AC770B58783AB02F.description: Recognize that animals and plants require care and begin to associate feeding and watering with the growth of humans, animals, and plants.

366C20669507470983E41080527F581B.description: Observe and explore growth and changes in humans, animals, and plants and demonstrate an under­standing that living things change over time in size and in other capacities as they grow.

682A59FF30434495B871A9693D8BC50C.description:
Indicate knowledge of the difference
between animate and inanimate
objects, providing greater detail,
and recognize that only animals and
plants undergo biological processes
such as growth, illness, healing,
and dying.

8C2609C740F44317B8ADAF76F1BF61A8.description:
Recognize that living things have
habitats in different environments
suited to their unique needs

1B930F5C6F6549598B91C51F56AF563C.description:
Indicate greater knowledge of body
parts and processes (e.g., eating,
sleeping, breathing, walking) in
humans and other animals.

6DCED5B375B74BF4B5CB24BBF2805EFA.description:
Identify characteristics of a greater
variety of animals and plants and
demonstrate an increased ability
to categorize them.

598F7110036E4637B6DFC244CEE1859F.description:
Indicate knowledge of the difference
between animate objects (animals,
people) and inanimate objects. For
example, expect animate objects
to initiate movement and to have
different insides than inanimate
objects.

F94C7F31FEEB491393EC25A7910E1F93.description:
Identify the habitats of people and
familiar animals and plants in the
environment and begin to realize that
living things have habitats in different
environments.

9C0B594DEDF243399D3D820E3746A61A.description:
Begin to indicate knowledge of body
parts and processes (e.g., eating,
sleeping, breathing, walking) in
humans and other animals.2

52395D6136034965A0BEF8262C77A62C.description:
Identify characteristics of a variety
of animals and plants, including
appearance (inside and outside) and
behavior, and begin to categorize
them.

491A0AC5205F4173BA50F6C07DA69398.description: Properties and Characteristics of Living Things

7F4347D875A64B399EE18A0097286A6E.description:
Demonstrate an increased ability to observe and describe in greater detail the motion of objects (in terms of speed, direction, the ways things move), and to explore the effect of own actions on the motion of objects,
including changes in speed and
direction.

3FF89983C51C4A028E4099B4D6603097.description: Demonstrate an increased awareness that objects and materials can change in various ways. Explore and describe in greater detail changes in objects and materials (rearrangement of parts; change in color, shape, texture, form, and temperature).

FC38F2F550274DE68D13EB0CE71E5180.description: Observe and describe the motion of objects (in terms of speed, direction, the ways things move), and explore the effect of own actions (e.g., pushing pulling, rolling, dropping) on making objects move.

96B79DB773A64BD4846346113D1ED8C7.description: Demonstrate awareness that objects and materials can change; explore and describe changes in objects and materials (rearrangement of parts; change in color, shape, texture, temperature).

2C88EC45A56A4A0CA203D5E88F936BA9.description: Changes in Nonliving Objects and Materials

D2A5D23D8FCA415A8993059F87C07D94.description:
Demonstrate increased ability to
observe, investigate, and describe in
greater detail the characteristics and
physical properties of objects and
of solid and nonsolid materials (size,
weight, shape, color, texture, and
sound).

AE310FF56EFB43F2935F96CC3B6E3936.description:
Observe, investigate, and identify
the characteristics and physical
properties of objects and of solid
and nonsolid materials (size, weight,
shape, color, texture, and sound).

14435C1C11344791A45D9223A8DC0B34.description:
Properties and Characteristics of Nonliving Objects
and Materials

664F24177D5D4C8786BB298D9CDAF2D3.description:
Share findings and explanations,
which may be correct or incorrect,
more spontaneously and with greater
detail.

8CE330C56BFA46B99CEA6527B7EF0DEB.description:
Record information more regularly
and in greater detail in various ways,
with adult assistance, including
pictures, words (dictated to adults),
charts, journals, models, photos, or
by tallying and graphing information.

AF9AA1149F5444798921DCB0A0E0C434.description:
Share findings and explanations,
which may be correct or incorrect,
with or without adult prompting.

D5971FF3811944CA897CC2DEF99022B7.description:
Record observations or findings in
various ways, with adult assistance,
including pictures, words (dictated to
adults), charts, journals, models, and
photos.

E73E291F8F244FEDBFD32EE80230167F.description:
Demonstrate an increased ability
to make inferences and form
generalizations based on evidence.

C2FB09BE2FEE4418B7B78E5AFDD25DF8.description:
Demonstrate an increased ability to
make predictions and check them
(e.g., may make more complex
predictions, offer ways to test
predictions, and discuss why
predictions were correct or incorrect).

91594A0D160D4037889F8A0746C2EFF0.description:
Compare and contrast objects and
events and describe similarities and
differences in greater detail.

3DD67BF8446C49DFA75B1EAB00AEBDC3.description:
Identify and use a greater variety
of observation and measurement
tools. May spontaneously use an
appropriate tool, though may still
need adult support.

5347246AA5F64F45B7C3B97A0C10FA1E.description:
Observe objects and events in the
environment and describe them in
greater detail.

ADE360CA8CCB464997172AA09CF6FAC3.description:
Demonstrate curiosity and an
increased ability to raise questions
about objects and events in their
environment.

F4F72812DF0F489DA89623649B674F5C.description: Make inferences and form generalizations based on evidence.

2D680DAF373447499EFB17B7791531B3.description:
Make predictions and check them,
with adult support, through concrete
experiences.

2A9B9B5429184227BB09E59B3F8F849D.description:
Compare and contrast objects
and events and begin to describe
similarities and differences.

7842B2C2F8764986B1E23DAA457E3E0F.description:
Begin to identify and use, with adult
support, some observation and
measurement tools.

8D6BEB452C9E4AF186E131D845800ECA.description:
Observe1
 objects and events in the
environment and describe them.

51EFE296A3D14C3BAF09861D061F07C8.description:
Demonstrate curiosity and raise
simple questions about objects and
events in their environment.

242C8771B4404DA9818F6C1E97A0166B.description:
Understand more complex economic
concepts (e.g., bartering; more
money is needed for things of
greater value; if more people want
something, more will be sold).

59CB064F30804A3896500091CF6CB238.description:
Understand ownership, limited
supply, what stores do, give-andtake, and payment of money to
sellers. Show interest in money and
its function, but still figuring out the
relative value of coins.

C05DBDD55F5A48AEA4E52C661B7DC42A.description:
Create their own drawings, maps,
and models; are more skilled at using
globes, maps, and map symbols;
and use maps for basic problem
solving (such as locating objects)
with adult guidance.

39184FBA7F7844DEA3770190CD82D988.description:
Can use drawings, globes, and
maps to refer to the physical world,
although often unclear on the use
of map symbols.
