547776ADCA774B029C35F470F2DAD121.description:
Show an interest in a wider range of
natural phenomena, including those
not directly experienced (such as
snow for a child living in Southern
California), and are more concerned
about caring for the natural world
and the positive and negative
impacts of people on the natural
world (e.g., recycling, putting trash
in trash cans).

940D0AF64E8049AAAF4AC84DA22DD227.description:
Show an interest in nature (including
animals, plants, and weather)
especially as children have direct
experience with them. Begin to
understand human interactions with
the environment (such as pollution in
a lake or stream) and the importance
of taking care of plants and animals.

256DA56F637C4B8299DB7EECB6868219.description:
Comprehend larger familiar locations, such as the characteristics of
their community and region (including
hills and streams, weather, common
activities) and the distances between
familiar locations (such as between
home and school), and compare
their home community with those
of others.

FE5251FC44544100A3CB605378643EF6.description:
Identify the characteristics of familiar
locations such as home and school,
describe objects and activities associated with each, recognize the
routes between them, and begin
using simple directional language
(with various degrees of accuracy).

59FA3B9DB201438AB75AB67AB3099A68.description:
Develop an interest in family history
(e.g., when family members were
children) as well as events of “long
ago,” and begin to understand when
these events occurred in relation to
each other.

C4A88A980B5F4926876852F355186637.description:
Easily distinguish older family
members from younger ones
(and other people) and events in
the recent past from those that
happened “long ago,” although
do not readily sequence historical
events on a timeline.

3F7BF1A3FB1440E4AD19141F18560F44.description: Historical Changes in People and the World

1E48953F05434B0DAAB291EE3F055F71.description:
Compare current abilities with skills
at a younger age and share more
detailed autobiographical stories
about recent experiences.

5458D60619474E9AA6EFDAD253D383E7.description:
Proudly display developing skills
to attract adult attention and share
simple accounts about recent
experiences.

C19D828EBCD74E4EB397381A89334A9D.description:
Distinguish when future events will
happen, plan for them, and make
choices (with adult assistance) that
anticipate future needs.

C86B37DB9B9E4AF58B5C808A416BCFD5.description:
Anticipate events in familiar
situations in the near future, with
adult assistance.

BF26F29F1B2D46B2ADD15EA3400E24F6.description:
Show improving ability to relate
past events to other past events
and current experiences, although
adult assistance continues to be
important.

E9FF43A4BCEE4FA29975E49915024933.description:
Recall past experiences easily and
enjoy hearing stories about the past,
but require adult help to determine
when past events occurred in relation
to each other and to connect them
with current experience.

89A89967A57444ECBCCCDE4F9D40E9B2.description:
More capable of negotiating,
compromising, and finding
cooperative means of resolving
conflict with peers or adults,
although verbal aggression may
also result.

FF4BAB8582F14715983F9B573C5D5D7B.description:
Can use simple bargaining strategies
and seek adult assistance when in
conflict with other children or adults,
although frustration, distress, or
aggression also occurs.

74C3825604AB40D6B9BF3C6493B3D36C.description:
Pay attention to others’ feelings,
more likely to provide assistance,
and try to coordinate personal
desires with those of other children in
mutually satisfactory ways. Actively
support rules that protect fairness to
others.

B3A50F13462E4A3A832CB8FC5B033C8A.description:
Respond to the feelings and needs
of others with simple forms of
assistance, sharing, and turn-taking.
Understand the importance of rules
that protect fairness and maintain
order.

7CB8B90C1BB842A3A81F6C807EB3C5AA.description: Fairness and Respect for Other People

C8A902DBD3BD4AA18EC38FBD0FE5BEEC.description:
Exhibit responsible conduct more
reliably as children develop selfesteem (and adult approval) from
being responsible group members.
May also manage others’ behavior
to ensure that others also fit in with
group expectations.

8C48B3ADFC0D48A4856C25CA00FDB7F8.description:
Strive to cooperate with group
expectations to maintain adult
approval and get along with others.
Self control is inconsistent, however - ,
especially when children are frustrated or upset.

3542F2E46246459988E09CEF17D92E6A.description:
Become involved as responsible
participants in group activities,
with growing understanding of the
importance of considering others’
opinions, group decision making,
and respect for majority rules and
the views of group members who
disagree with the majority.

590F8CE47F57465A9E5E0E6117FAC8B2.description:
Identify as members of a group,
participate willingly in group
activities, and begin to understand
and accept responsibility as group
members, although assistance is
required in coordinating personal
interests with those of others.

D1458D746095448891A9B1DFD16FBB03.description: Exhibit more sophisticated understanding of a broader variety of adult roles and occupations, but uncertain how work relates to income.

C32B729E4F704F9DA5A1E1D287312997.description: Play familiar adult social roles and occupations (such as parent, teacher, and doctor) consistent with their developing knowledge of these roles.

540511A152064686AD8349F40CBF58C9.description:
Understand the mutual responsibilities
of relationships; take initiative in
developing relationships that are
mutual, cooperative, and exclusive.

1D0DB579217B4DF89035B25152163B74.description:
Interact comfortably with many
peers and adults; actively contribute
to creating and maintaining relationships with a few significant adults
and peers.

6874653F054B4B859A3BBB67F76B8F51.description: Manifest stronger cultural, ethnic, and racial identity and greater familiarity with relevant language, traditions, and other practices. Show more interest in human diversity, but strongly favor characteristics of their own group.

673F1B6566A74CEB87912845600B0EBF.description: Exhibit developing cultural, ethnic, and racial identity and understand relevant language and cultural practices. Display curiosity about diversity in human characteristics and practices, but prefer those of their own group.

document.title: Computer Science Standards for California Public Schools Kindergarten through Grade Twelve

450E8FF5DE994550B5E4E82220993818.description:
Compare tradeoffs between allowing
information to be public and keeping
information private and secure.

70A4BD4CB37D489397023D50DA8EB252.description:
Compare tradeoffs associated with
licenses for computational artifacts to
balance the protection of the creators’
rights and the ability for others to use
and modify the artifacts.

485CDFD934F241C1A3B33535ECAC4174.description:
Collaborate with many contributors
when creating a computational
artifact.

4B0434AE8CF04220AE86258CC9CB596D.description:
Discuss issues of bias and
accessibility in the design of existing
technologies.

D6DFAE6B5F224CDFA14616E54AB285EA.description:
Compare tradeoffs associated with
computing technologies that affect
people’s everyday activities and
career options.

594E64AA20004901B4C6432ABD76A9BC.description:
Document programs in order to make
them easier to use, read, test, and
debug.

F4D35650A5254103B07A4D2E7743701B.description:
Distribute tasks and maintain a
project timeline when collaboratively
developing computational artifacts.

63260ABD192B4192ACDA52593B9BD936.description:
Systematically test and refine
programs using a range of test cases.

99D5E048C04046EF83EEC7478F6D4DAC.description:
Incorporate existing code, media, and
libraries into original programs, and
give attribution.

9EFC0150B57A4591A3273664A070677A.description:
Seek and incorporate feedback from
team members and users to refine a
solution that meets user needs.

D832B81B79874ADDA67FB6A784826341.description:
Create procedures with parameters to
organize code and make it easier to
reuse.

DE33B30AAB3E488896ADB276A2ED47AB.description:
Decompose problems and
subproblems into parts to facilitate
the design, implementation, and
review of programs.

C5EC95E12D57418998AFAB4A76A3AD12.description:
Design and iteratively develop
programs that combine control
structures and use compound
conditions.

B4A840DBE95247B4832B7A7284F76F00.description:
Create clearly named variables that
store data, and perform operations on
their contents.

AB316BA9A4F54442ABF3C060C59C3B33.description:
Use flowcharts and/or pseudocode to
design and illustrate algorithms that
solve complex problems.

F7C98916632842D4A1946DA6BFCC225E.description:
Test and analyze the effects of
changing variables while using
computational models.

3ABB9D7AA0F94EAFACA01B5244E5E859.description:
Collect data using computational
tools and transform the data to make
it more useful.

4843F7EC4B8F4DC591A705A596AA7811.description:
Apply multiple methods of information
protection to model the secure
transmission of information.

EC44D00353E54677804454D0A4888DBE.description:
Explain potential security threats and
security measures to mitigate threats.

80670BE4E1F54882A48EA0594FB5326A.description:
Model the role of protocols in
transmitting data across networks and
the internet.

448500CB634D4C85A2B415E510D8BCD2.description:
Systematically apply troubleshooting
strategies to identify and resolve
hardware and software problems in
computing systems.

FDF7BDF3FA3945CD87B56F395847D88B.description:
Design a project that combines
hardware and software components
to collect and exchange data.

33D0A5E65C77484FB25CF70B9269A2EF.description:
Design modifications to computing
devices in order to improve the ways
users interact with the devices.

document.title: Computer Science Standards for California Public Schools Kindergarten through Grade Twelve

F1E41C17CD7F473399533A3B63B8294F.description:
Evaluate the social and economic
implications of privacy in the context
of safety, law, or ethics.

1E1BD8C0FBEA4CFA8C83950BF5BA3652.description:
Explain the privacy concerns related
to the collection and generation of
data through automated processes.

78495298933F4590B3F0FE275F066DCF.description:
Explain the beneficial and harmful
effects that intellectual property laws
can have on innovation.

4AC2F25825D74026A41FC78B185CEAC5.description:
Use collaboration tools and methods
to increase connectivity with people
of different cultures and careers.

BAD1282924934350ADAD59CC517CE72F.description:
Study, discuss, and think critically
about the potential impacts and
implications of emerging technologies
on larger social, economic, and
political structures, with evidence
from credible sources.

DFD4ED7595F349A9AB88DED9BED5EC21.description:
Demonstrate ways a given algorithm
applies to problems across
disciplines.

35DF41E83B844E628D03327D5BE3AD0C.description:
Identify impacts of bias and equity
deficit on design and implementation
of computational artifacts and apply
appropriate processes for evaluating
issues of bias.

677DF9C6716942158C04E4D25FBFC41C.description:
Evaluate the ways computing impacts
personal, ethical, social, economic,
and cultural practices.

BE840BA3FE54460DA8FD32763F7AA370.description:
Document decisions made during the
design process using text, graphics,
presentations, and/or demonstrations
in the development of complex
programs.

73737622B81F485CA013D23DE6A7E147.description:
Design and develop computational
artifacts working in team roles using
collaborative tools.

B3DBC8A9A62E417787039A7CAD8097F7.description:
Iteratively evaluate and refine a
computational artifact to enhance its
performance, reliability, usability, and
accessibility.

2750BA36A9EF4EDF925990ABEF6E3C53.description:
Explain the limitations of licenses
that restrict use of computational
artifacts when using resources such
as libraries.

9C6F116D60FB46298D199C6C8BDC446E.description:
Systematically design programs for
broad audiences by incorporating
feedback from users.

8AE41AE2D8D54AFBB7434744EACC240F.description:
Create computational artifacts using
modular design.

7741A675C9464612874489B86B17CF9D.description:
Decompose problems into smaller
subproblems through systematic
analysis, using constructs such as
procedures, modules, and/or classes.

A49B3EC0DC4D4FB1B2BA680D725F0F5A.description:
Iteratively design and develop
computational artifacts for practical
intent, personal expression, or to
address a societal issue by using
events to initiate instructions.

EA6D00DDC215464CA66A1E44993A1F55.description:
Justify the selection of specific control
structures by identifying tradeoffs
associated with implementation,
readability, and performance.

30D0C9F10FBC4965A545ED4FB047F1E3.description:
Create more generalized
computational solutions using
collections instead of repeatedly
using simple variables.

B37EE0E990B6422181ED535B593E5FB7.description:
Design algorithms to solve
computational problems using a
combination of original and existing
algorithms.

3A0CA5C66D99473D832BFE2DB52CAB2C.description:
Refine computational models to
better represent the relationships
among different elements of data
collected from a phenomenon or
process.

E55B4DB09F2D477A82AB27AF3F7C5194.description:
Create data visualizations to help
others better understand real-world
phenomena.

FFA01FF72A6C48B48E5F8F519095FC27.description:
Describe tradeoffs associated with
how data elements are organized and
stored.

A649B62E132E4FE0A6CC20349DE2A653.description:
Translate between different
representations of data abstractions
of real-world phenomena, such as
characters, numbers, and images.

24134040DA6447E6A06F62D5F29D5125.description:
Compare and contrast cryptographic
techniques to model the secure
transmission of information.

3270DC3413C541538DF12EC32C7F440C.description:
Compare and contrast security
measures to address various security
threats.

A61EFADAC0B94A42A395036AC02072C5.description:
Describe the design characteristics of
the internet.

EC900694A7F1428D9E777F88E78447DC.description:
Describe issues that impact network
functionality.

88849A33E1C24824B572FE0A33A199B2.description:
Develop guidelines that convey
systematic troubleshooting strategies
that others can use to identify and fix
errors.

7E013C0437D2402F9D62B07DF269B3EF.description:
Compare levels of abstraction and
interactions between application
software, system software, and
hardware.

190674E748424D5DB36F8C1F887AF865.description:
Describe ways in which abstractions
hide the underlying implementation
details of computing systems to
simplify user experiences.

document.title: Computer Science Standards for California Public Schools Kindergarten through Grade Twelve

513D5632C5044BB797BD797C14539E3F.description:
Debate laws and regulations that
impact the development and use of
software.

46EE0731F6844D9D954E596EFD0C8A58.description:
Evaluate the impact of equity, access,
and influence on the distribution
of computing resources in a global
society.

88B0CC844E324EDEB7E9D6B4119D7DAF.description:
Evaluate how computational
innovations that have revolutionized
aspects of our culture might evolve.

5FC2953B32024CD7B48E7950F6B67A12.description:
Evaluate computational artifacts with
regard to improving their beneficial
effects and reducing harmful effects
on society.

E78C3BE89E3A46F9AC7826DDF0B686D4.description:
Compare multiple programming
languages, and discuss how their
features make them suitable for
solving different types of problems.

2E784B25C67F464998DE17F1DE6389B9.description:
Use version control systems,
integrated development environments
(IDEs), and collaborative tools and
practices (e.g., code documentation)
while developing software within a
group.

F7DF15C874184DCC90EF10C0892803F6.description:
Evaluate key qualities of a program
through a process such as a code
review.

119AD766DC4443BDA74FF23C3D9DBEC1.description:
Modify an existing program to
add additional functionality and
discuss intended and unintended
implications.

DC2D1663C2FA467A87B689DABB958A20.description:
Develop and use a series of test
cases to verify that a program
performs according to its design
specifications.

1A50390687AA441E9FB23BE3E82BA733.description:
Identify and fix security issues
that might compromise computer
programs.

E356BEA39E0A42D5BA45AF990827CB92.description:
Develop programs for multiple
computing platforms.

0827F69B942548669952E96990C74EE8.description:
Plan and develop programs for broad
audiences using a specific software
life cycle process.

93308DF9146F4BCF9CB17F8E68BBC515.description:
Demonstrate code reuse by creating
programming solutions using libraries
and APIs.

97B32968C1264DA7A38E9A7A773596F9.description:
Construct solutions to problems using
student-created components, such as
procedures, modules, and/or objects.

BF10BD981D364CD3A042BD8D22B8AE45.description:
Analyze a large-scale computational
problem and identify generalizable
patterns or problem components that
can be applied to a solution.

B50C938B09494435BF8AC5B422FF3A7A.description:
Demonstrate the flow of execution of
a recursive algorithm.

1D702FD0893D4B7495EB801B36F987F3.description:
Compare and contrast fundamental
data structures and their uses.

88C9B08726C04174AF976F7566534AB0.description:
Evaluate algorithms in terms of their
efficiency.

22620B7408BB4ED494843B6401896FC9.description:
Implement searching and sorting
algorithms to solve computational
problems.

1EDFC80A663D4E5BBCF0DA140195CD21.description:
Implement an algorithm that uses
artificial intelligence to overcome a
simple challenge.

C33B3CF26DDF485C9322B0903E4E4552.description:
Describe how artificial intelligence
drives many software and physical
systems.

7759CDA69F31487B8CAB770716910595.description:
Evaluate the ability of models and
simulations to test and support the
refinement of hypotheses.

9976AAE1D2394810BE654FCC2EF65FDD.description:
Use data analysis tools and
techniques to identify patterns in data
representing complex systems.

87633B76AE174568990D3756FC468BA0.description:
Select and use data collection tools
and techniques to generate data sets.

CFB313298E854F23B8A2245BD0F0A35D.description:
Analyze cryptographic techniques
to model the secure transmission of
information.

B55ADB279AE14F1BAD84AF23E645A9DB.description:
Explain how the characteristics of
the internet influence the systems
developed on it.

9D7D0F9721B3464AB17F983ABCD2BC9C.description:
Examine the scalability and
reliability of networks, by describing
the relationship between routers,
switches, servers, topology, and
addressing.

F09AF20FA2B6422E843E7BF8A4482224.description:
Categorize and describe the different
functions of operating system
software.

398E5130161C44DABBEAFB1D551AD24C.description:
Illustrate ways computing systems
implement logic through hardware
components.

and appropriately
with media
arts tools and

Context to Deepen Understanding

share experiences
of media artworks.

experiences in

artworks.

examine and share
appealing qualities
in media artworks.

D00A937336444D5180AD7220411A3CA8.description:

media artworks.

With guidance,
explore media
artworks and
discuss experiences.

With guidance,
explore and discuss
components and
messages in a
variety of media
artworks.

and participate in

audience.

creative skills,
such as imagining,
freely and in
guided practice,
within media arts
productions.

F444A7B4BB574F579F39EB1B16B18439.description:
Use identified
skills, such as
manipulating tools,
making choices,
and sharing, in
creating media
artworks.

F5EA68AE8AD64EF08E4BC6ED0D70635D.description: Develop and Refine Artistic Techniques and Work for Presentation

F632F8004F63405AA4B1EDC6CE4725ED.description:

combine different
forms and content,

sound, to form
media artworks.

848AD762D5E54BA88E008FF7F0933BB3.description: Select, Analyze, and Interpret Artistic Work for Presentation

90F032EA371943FCBF9317F40F3A292F.description:
Attempt and
share expressive
effects, freely and
in guided practice,
in creating media
artworks.

535B982BDDFE47BEB95F0D7CB8219344.description:
Make and capture
media arts content,
freely and in guided

arts productions.

B2C0478C54FA4D6983ABFC3CA7C5A2CA.description:

ideas into plans or

arts productions.

methods, and

Share appealing
qualities and

With guidance,
share observations
regarding a variety
of media artworks.

DFC23401B5B942D29BE7F19697F8C8B8.description: Interpret Intent and Meaning in Artistic Work

Recognize and

experiences.

F91C2F0430DD49A4BBF3388031573419.description:
Recognize and
share components
and messages in
media artworks.

With guidance,
discuss the

media artworks.

8C7122DDC4CF45BFBFB706FBD064CBA7.description: Convey Meaning Through the Presentation of Artistic Work

Identify and
demonstrate
creative skills, such
as performing,
within media arts
productions.

FF0F502473F641AA801674985493C1FA.description:
Identify and
demonstrate basic

handling tools,

Make changes to
the content, form,
or presentation of

share results.

Form and capture

Students are able to negotiate across differences and find mutually satisfactory compromises where appropriate.

6C6B36BB3C6A40B9A8943DECCF3B9763.description: Students can participate in harm reparation by using restorative affective statements and restorative questions in order to communicate the impact of harm and hold community members accountable for their actions. Students are able to take responsibility for their own actions and can contribute to the collaborative process of harm reparation.

BDD2C361029C4CDCA57310B7DE37BE4C.description: Students recognize the value of collaborative problem solving and actively engaging in empathic listening, respectfully communicating, and honoring equity of voice in order to find solutions and achieve a common goal.

47143EEF23E64D8189FED40CA1787C88.description: Students can identify and affirm the rich cultural diversity that exists in their community, state, and country. Students demonstrate appreciation for, curiosity about, and a willingness to better understand those who are different from them. Students maintain cultural humility through reflection and self-critique.

0BBF9B0F93964B00A0086B429C45B767.description: Students recognize the value of trust, rapport, and respect in developing healthy relationships across different racial, cultural, linguistic, gender, sexual orientation, religious, ability, and neurodivergent student groups. Students recognize the characteristics of healthy and unhealthy dating relationships. Students use a variety of culturally affirming strategies to show appreciation and gratitude to their peers and social networks.

B542DB427BF24481B50F630B088FD148.description: Students seek out leadership opportunities that are meaningful to them. Students recognize group dynamics, including power structures. Students participate in distributive leadership processes that leverage their cultural identity and lived experience.

B6A8F2F1570B4A39BE2098826102E070.description: Students recognize the influence of negative peer pressure and actively work to assertively reject unwanted and unhealthy pressures.

standardSets.title: Social Awareness: High School
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Social Awareness

D71239F12E854F0283733FDA58D08EDD.description: Students identify and understand interconnected inequities in their community, state, and country and engage in civic, community, or service projects that support community empowerment and equity.

DA30F1EE9FDA4091B40E67920B0F1EB4.description: Students are deepening their knowledge about how power and privilege can perpetuate inequities. Students understand the historical and ongoing individual and institutional impacts of bias, racism, misogyny, inequality, and patterns of injustice, including the rights of different groups.

3C634B6F7AC94B16A4EBD16E60AD79CD.description: Students demonstrate inclusion by identifying learning community members that are or feel marginalized and centering those voices in order to deepen belonging for all. Students identify and interrupt group dynamics when they impede belonging.

151257A26EA5420AB196FA37DD9D8DEB.description: Students identify and navigate different support networks. Students are advocates and allies for others' needs and recognize the interdependence of community resources.

C430BB64ABC64AE783DE27F70183D9EC.description:
Students take the lead to actualize the components of a relationship-
centered, caring, inclusive, and just community and engage in practices to co-construct and maintain a learning environment where all students’ voices are heard and honored. Students contribute to diversifying the curriculum.

6F74B5B795D1463DBA4DCD070167D033.description: Students acknowledge and validate others’ emotions and lived experiences and challenge their own assumptions about others’ feeling states based on their dispositions, expressiveness, race, or cultural backgrounds. Students explore the perspectives of others, whether they agree or not, with curiosity and extend empathy, care, and compassion.

FE35861A00D045478052AD752E30CDCD.description: Students build and analyze their knowledge of cultural, racial, linguistic, class, gender, ability, and other types of identity and how those identities are shaped by, and perceived, in society. Students can recognize and honor strengths in all people.

standardSets.title: Social Awareness: Adult
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Social Awareness

B7862B9BE54D45678109D8ADD94DE9F4.description: Adults model how to contribute to one's community by sharing their passion and the process of identifying and collaboratively addressing inequities.

23FB3905545E48FE9AB45EF4663D7A0D.description: Adults can identify and explain how power and privilege can perpetuate inequities and contribute to marginalization. Adults are aware of the historical and current inequities and the social issues of the community in which they work or live.

AE053403BB174E2895261185D9368648.description: Adults are aware of the ways group and power dynamics can help or impede learning, development, and inclusion. Adults elevate marginalized voices to increase a sense of belonging for all.

34BCF7C110C54C8693B9B1F69C581993.description: Adults model and normalize accessing resources and assistance. They mentor students to become engaged, informed, and supportive community members.

FC872A9C424B42DD809EBAF369AC86CF.description: Adults prioritize diversifying the curriculum, building trusting relationships, and creating an intentional learning community centered on compassion and respect. Adults understand that you have to reach and engage students before you teach them every day and in every subject. Adults support students to take ownership of the learning environment, including creating clear community agreements. Adults work to create brave spaces that use reflective listening and honor both differences and commonalities.

13D36045DE8F42D6B42369B86C5A71DF.description: Adults recognize that all teaching and learning is social and emotional. Adults acknowledge that the historical, political, cultural, community, and family experiences that students bring to the learning environment influence the way students express and perceive emotions. Adults show empathy, stay curious, and strive to understand the actions and perspectives of students and other adults.

1AFEE017541A4974A76665117EFBC6F7.description: Adults acknowledge that the dominant culture of schools and society, among other factors, often puts students from marginalized backgrounds at risk of stress, alienation, and disengagement. Adults recognize the genius of all students, peers, and families; elevate commonalities and connections; and celebrate differences between diverse groups.

standardSets.title: Social Awareness: Middle School
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Social Awareness

BDBDEF0C8BC94FEBA4EC80634156A68A.description: Students accurately recognize inequities and community needs and collaborate with adults and peers to take action on real world issues in support of a more inclusive, caring, healthy, and just community.

947CB85AE2A7413E8F741EAF16A0C446.description: Students examine and reflect on how individuals act on their explicit and implicit bias, how some policies can contribute to injustice, and the damaging impact this can have on others and our society. Students explore intent versus impact.

48E1CD062AD54775A0D9A2D36B531B3F.description: Students reflect on how to build an accepting and inclusive learning community. Students collaborate to identify barriers to belonging for all individuals in their learning community. Students question the norms of groups and systems in healthy ways.

F057F96E6FF74C92B3544ABAEEA578E2.description: Students know when and where to proactively seek resources and supports and begin to understand the interdependence of members of a community.

94A15DA6C4E548948F99B641F892ED50.description: Students co-construct all aspects of relationship-centered, just, and caring learning environments, including shared agreements and norms for engagement. Students question the inclusivity of the curriculum.

B887231F76A64438988B11B69AD6B56E.description: Students explore differences in emotional expression and communication norms across cultures and communities and how differences can contribute to misunderstandings, but also provide opportunity for growth. Students respond compassionately to others’ experiences and demonstrate care and concern.

E65DAD12DA884F15A02D7A798CF84A80.description: Students reflect on how social identities (e.g., cultural, racial, class, gender, linguistic, ability) impact the way people view and interact with others, including those from diverse groups.

standardSets.title: Social Awareness: Late Elementary
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Social Awareness

BB7CC06B56D4472B8EEF26DC28945F18.description: Students explore the importance and power of community participation and service. Students collaborate with others to identify ways to contribute productively to their learning community.

B8A9FF14FCE5431BAA220CD235F6A3B7.description: Students can work cooperatively in a diverse group of peers. Students identify their own basic rights and the rights of others. Students begin to understand how bias, prejudice, stereotypes, and racism can play a role in how people act and make decisions. Students can give examples of how these issues can disrupt or harm groups in our society.

F8FD2E462A7F4C5A909BE0F9B2C0C4EE.description: Students demonstrate acceptance and inclusion of those who are different from themselves and value the contributions of the members of a diverse group.

E35699BEBD5149F3826E6A9862FFEE40.description: Students identify appropriate, trusted people to seek support from based on their specific needs and recognize ways they can support others.

936CDEAC134C4EFC852C274CEC64CE69.description: Students recognize healthy and safe boundaries in interactions with others in their family, learning community, and beyond. Students identify strategies to build and maintain trust.

50E8AD24E67241E7A39831ACE5032DB3.description: Students name ways people’s identities and experiences may lead to different emotional reactions. Students show curiosity about and strive to take the perspective of others based on what they know about that person or group. Students show empathy and compassion for others.

C37E2F0ECB73428BB60BFB013415B382.description: Students identify opinions versus facts about people and groups who are similar and different from themselves. Students name specific strengths and assets of individuals from diverse groups.

standardSets.title: Social Awareness: Early Elementary
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Social Awareness

A21E00532827407C9E0732F2C912257E.description: Students name ways that they can contribute to or participate in groups and communities and how they can be helpful, fair, compassionate, and respectful to those in other groups or communities.

734D84C54B67459B808E6F15A7AD0B6E.description: Students describe and demonstrate fairness toward others. Students can describe how rules can benefit some people over others. Students cooperate and play with peers respectfully.

0F439B180E374493BD2D747502E70DD2.description: Students name groups or communities they are a part of and their qualities. Students demonstrate pride in belonging to their groups or communities and take action to make others feel welcome.

FD2F01A100AE4A5FA92484691DAA6FF9.description: Students describe what it means to be a helpful community member. Students can identify people in their learning environment and family that can support them when they need help.

FD8B09D42DA346A98B3D234CC9A146B8.description: Students contribute to creating and maintaining shared agreements that guide their interactions with others and their environment. Students show kindness toward people of all backgrounds and experiences.

7FD8E35CC15B42A9888CCB2AEE681EA2.description: Students recognize and name emotions in others using verbal and physical cues. Students describe how others may feel in a variety of situations and show empathy for others’ experiences.

8A7F8DBA46E04AEEA9630E97635E13D3.description: Students discuss similarities and differences between themselves and others and different social and cultural groups.

standardSets.title: Self-Management: Early Elementary
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Management

8CA9D5C5929F4E009D3543A5CD037A62.description: Students keep their spaces and belongings organized with guidance.

5D42A1E1D33B45E89CFDB849F967B5E2.description: Students begin practicing self-monitoring thoughts and actions and asking for help to stay motivated and focused. Students are aware of their body during active listening. Students are able to identify when they are focused and paying attention.

6A53FE2A2DE14E53B02E2B971377478F.description: Students identify personal and collective goals and name simple steps to achieve them.

9CDDD159C786492783365951C28642B0.description: Students understand and practice maintaining others’ stated emotional and physical boundaries.

2E32C85EE8EE44A6A539108A96CCFD92.description: Students understand the purpose of feedback and can listen to and accept simple, constructive feedback.

515CD4B5EF53482D868BF0EAEA19CEC3.description: Students identify and practice strategies they have used or can use to stay hopeful and “bounce back” from challenges.

1BEBB421C87443CD8E79EC6DB665C435.description: Students identify situations and relationships that calm them. Students understand and begin to practice how to be physically healthy in ways that are within their control.

5D7242B5AD89490D9760FC805F1575C8.description: Students practice noticing their emotions, where they experience them in their bodies, and using those signs to choose strategies to express feelings in helpful ways. Students practice strategies that help them to sustain joy and feel calmer, patient, focused and energized.

standardSets.title: Self-Management: Late Elementary
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Management

60DED13499324213B5352545BE5E0441.description: Students practice managing their own time, organizing their materials, and gathering what is needed for a task or activity.

202C609A3BCD4DBBAD51936555F82E40.description: Students use personally relevant strategies, like self-talk, to get and stay motivated. Students can identify distractions and know and apply simple solutions to overcome them.

198F3BD4D9E047A5B619FB364E4187AF.description: Students identify short- and longer-term personal and collective goals that are meaningful to them and demonstrate strategies that work for them to achieve those goals.

26356014588B49D88808C93142CF61AC.description: Students perceive social cues and resist impulses in order to maintain the explicit or implied emotional and physical boundaries of others.

9E9209CA01E7428CBE0560B822960B61.description: Students welcome constructive feedback and understand and use varied strategies to give feedback to peers.

A440A3CB50904EB6A28192D292D804AD.description: Students describe different types of adversity and what they can learn from others’ stories of overcoming difficult experiences, resilience, and remaining hopeful in the face of challenges (e.g., current and historical characters).

BAE911E2550D45B6A772488A995AB67E.description: Students know and use simple stress management practices. Students engage in mental and physical health promoting activities in ways that are within their control.

DD9A54D4AAF04789A4144855D4F7B9E7.description: Students practice self-monitoring and harness and express their emotions in authentic and constructive ways by identifying, articulating, and using emotional regulation strategies that work for them. Students use diverse strategies to express themselves effectively in different social and cultural contexts.

standardSets.title: Self-Management: Middle School
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Management

40123D50CF694DADADD2B1BAFE173A5A.description: Students take an active role in managing their time, activities, and responsibilities.

9A7928BC74AB4F3EBC6D3DFD05C6EE5F.description: Students can create and follow routines, independently adapt to challenges and distractions, and apply perseverance strategies that work for them.

B75187DB37D445EF8AAC343626A12F68.description: Students identify and work toward incremental personal and collective goals in pursuit of longer-term, achievements. Students identify and commit to roles in achieving collective goals. Students begin to examine how to balance personal and collective goals.

132EBE27672F4721A180A74D44A716E9.description: Students reflect on their changing boundaries to support their growth and well-being. Students also examine and reflect on healthy boundaries within different cultures.

FC8733D03E19471B8853C4A0C5C6D03E.description: Students seek out and make changes based on constructive feedback and demonstrate contextually appropriate ways of giving feedback to peers, educators, and others in their learning community and family.

000A78F16B904D9C8E1B88C0B3F503B6.description: Students consider various paths through individual and collective adversity. Students reflect on their sources of inner strength, hope, and what they look for in supportive relationships.

6205175456F84359A1F772318986F65F.description: Students describe how stress affects their choices and actions and practice multiple strategies to manage stress. Students choose, take ownership of, and engage in activities that promote their mental and physical health.

2635849F9C1844CAADAD04264A8089FE.description: Students explore the difference between emotion suppression and management and how to channel emotions productively. Students work on reframing feelings before acting on them.

standardSets.title: Self-Management: High School
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Management

6CFD56AA739C422A87B20B27B73D3BFA.description: Students proactively use several time management strategies to organize their class work, extracurricular activities, work, family responsibilities, and other commitments.

D9C2FF384B9A40F999376716655E71AF.description: Students identify and apply a variety of culturally relevant and identity affirming strategies to stay motivated and disciplined in order to persevere in achieving their goals.

CA41CD0EAD994CCAB87EBE4684014B1C.description:
Students continuously strive toward meaningful,
specific personal short- and long-term goals. Students contribute to collective goal setting and achievement by identifying Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Relevant, Time-bound, Equity-Focused (SMARTE) goals. Students use their voice and choice to demonstrate personal and collective agency.

684439A4105948C99D732075710CD7AD.description: Students recognize healthy social, emotional, and physical boundaries and use cultural norms, environmental, and social context cues to navigate these boundaries.

0DB425310175435489F17C612ECED208.description: Students engage in regular constructive feedback loops with their peers and adults. Students can listen to critical feedback with an openness to learning and offer authentic, specific, culturally appropriate feedback that is supportive and nonjudgmental.

395AC1E465C443E2ACF7078D951AE62C.description: Students recognize the challenges of adverse life situations and the intersection of systems of injustice. Students leverage collective efficacy to cultivate resilience and hope.

94385B0D5BB8451180137857AA4225B0.description: Students proactively prepare for potentially stressful situations, recognize when they are dysregulated or stressed and know how to pause in order to effectively respond. Students regularly participate in mental and physical health promoting activities and use a variety of self-care strategies that are safe, culturally relevant, and affirming.

E451E7B53CA949C08028A86918CDC00A.description: Students deepen their capacity for emotional regulation by using a variety of culturally relevant practices to embrace and process strong emotions.

standardSets.title: Self-Awareness: Adult
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Awareness

18A087340CB74AF79943A5A77547B71E.description: Adults model a mastery orientation to learning, including the process of making mistakes, intellectual humility, practicing positive self-talk, and demonstrating optimism and a growth mindset.

DF5F3AF3F96D49398DD4678E0741178D.description: Adults model the process of how they have identified their strengths and personal power and how they use them to better serve their life purpose and the lives of others.

8F36414293674E7EA1ACB0DC62C8418A.description: Adults are able to identify the connections between a thought, feeling, and behavior, and interrupt the cycle that results in a negative consequence for self or others. Adults model cultural awareness around emotions.

CF07B6FCA51B4AF98F7DE08FC96E244A.description: Adults model being contributing, reflective, and caring community members with students and other adults in the learning community.

83372EE7D5474A4C8782B11D2BF5AFE8.description: Adults continually reflect on and interrupt their own prejudices and biases in regard to academic and behavioral expectations of students, including how those impact discipline, grading, giving leadership opportunities, and whose voices are heard in the learning environment.

908A270C2BBE4EE9B53BE76EEE21F6BA.description: Adults continuously reflect on and critically examine their own mental models, ideologies, and life experiences, and evaluate how these influence their beliefs and values.

722D553430B7459BA029C64E66458A69.description: Adults recognize, understand, label with granularity, and accept their emotions.

CB9C589E7E014C1ABB1C1AAFA07A389E.description: Adults have deep and accurate knowledge of their own identity and its implications for their role in supporting student development. Adults model continuous reflection and exploration of their own evolving identity.

standardSets.title: Self-Awareness: High School
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Awareness

0590D6EDF11142099DD2F1763C7F766E.description: Students deepen and build a more nuanced understanding of self-efficacy by embracing and leveraging mistakes as opportunities for growth, displaying a well-developed mastery orientation to learning.

842BF8F871934A6791EF7E2FA98EEDE6.description: Students identify and apply their personal strengths and assets to deepen their sense of power and pursue their purpose.

F9B586284D8B428B96753FFA91D4AA84.description: Students deepen their understanding of brain and body connections and how behavior is shaped by culture and lived experiences. Students can assess and respond to their environment by choosing to code-switch.

BE9DA5EBA1A8453A94CCC4D0C8A269CE.description: Students can assess and analyze areas of need in their community and make a plan to contribute. Students can reflect on the quality and impact of their community service and civic engagement.

493382D5F94744C2AB984EBFE1E6D64C.description: Students are regularly identifying and interrupting their own prejudices and implicit biases and reflecting on the impact on others.

E1584A3DAAEC48F987F1AD6B27FD97ED.description: Students deepen their understanding of their own perspectives, values, beliefs, and mental models. Students critically examine and question their own perspectives and opinions.

5456E57C03FF4EBE9BE90E314400EFAD.description: Students accurately label and understand their feeling states and can embrace strong emotions without judgment.

75F296E5BFC64E9089F19ADCD97BC1BE.description: Students work to understand multiple aspects of their identity including race, ethnicity, language, gender, and ability, among others, and how they intersect. Students recognize the evolving and dynamic nature of identity based on context and perceptions of self and others.

standardSets.title: Self-Awareness: Middle School
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Awareness

ED5775AF91534EE1AF44FA7A376F7280.description: Students examine and reflect on how beliefs about themselves and about learning intersect (mastery orientation versus performance orientation) and the impact on their optimism and confidence.

66959A67A2E34278ABE4C6CD6CD5CA12.description: Students develop a sense of personal power and can identify and use their personal, social, and cultural assets in healthy ways.

F9B8EB35F80D4573A1F593B0132CFCB7.description: Students recognize the connection between their thoughts, emotions, and behavior based on brain science. Students recognize how they express their emotions may be influenced by their culture and experiences.

8D6F022768494AC993D1A2879B34E4FA.description: Students begin to identify what they need from communities they belong to and assess if their needs are being met. Students are aware of the ways they are or are not meeting the needs of others in their learning community.

2E3DE4D83806458F9AA0571CC308F683.description: Students begin to identify their prejudices and biases and how those might impact their behaviors toward others related to being inclusive or exclusive.

A477DA1E829C47A8A9F6FB23BBA3860E.description: Students explore the concept of values: how they are formed, how they reflect our identity and experiences, and how they are applied. Students start to examine how personal perspectives and values can be challenged.

4E0101811CB04DDD97C58F3462715361.description: Students examine and reflect on the underlying causes of emotions. Students recognize the difference between emotions and feelings. Students work to label, with specificity, their feeling states.

B54D4DFB2DFA4530A74E5B1506425275.description: Students identify and explore their different social identities, including race, ethnicity, language, gender, and ability. Students begin to explore the concept of intersectionality. Students cultivate a healthy, well-grounded sense of self- confidence based on their strengths.

standardSets.title: Self-Awareness: Late Elementary
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Awareness

B85AABF486A14FF4891D5F4D87790708.description: Students are more accurate in their perceptions and gain confidence in their own thoughts and well-founded opinions but are open to trying and listening to new and different ideas.

DD85856758D647CF9B791200434292AA.description: Students articulate their needs in constructive ways. Students begin to develop a sense of personal purpose and feel that their lives are important and meaningful.

8C7A771611CE4FB298E7FC425AE030CF.description: Students recognize how their emotions are information they can choose to harness and use. Students understand that there are no “bad” emotions and that their feeling states can be changed intentionally.

DDFE9FF473D64132A568207FC3D24EFC.description: Students describe their roles and contributions in the different settings in which they participate. Students identify characteristics and habits they have and how they may affect others in their learning community.

F30A1719DBC7402085A1A878F4A59EF3.description:
Students are able to reflect on their own experiences of inclusion and
exclusion and of being excluded and
excluding others.

86E2884D2BF14B408C4B8C2D960890C3.description: Students articulate their beliefs about topics that are important to them, their family, and their learning community.

7C502AE59B3C411BBE8DE832779187F8.description: Students recognize the intensity of their emotions and can name increasingly complex emotions. Students identify when they feel stressed or anxious.

A17411441CD84648B3336AC3BB8D2A86.description: Students understand how some aspects of their personal and social identity can change over time and be shaped by themselves, others, and their experiences. Students show confidence and pride in their identity without needing to feel superior to others.

standardSets.title: Self-Awareness: Early Elementary
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Awareness

A4EB3C1BCBCF444580B43B68E1DA3C23.description: Students believe in their capacity to learn and that they are capable, important community members. Students practice having an optimistic outlook.

12ABCA4DABD945F6939B419413D743D6.description: Students are aware of, and distinguish between, their wants and needs. Students can name their strengths such as skills, knowledge, or talents.

B9B944752396482F8BB0C65B80EAB80E.description: Students reflect on experiences as the causes of certain emotions. Students recognize the purpose of emotions and name simple ways their emotions influence their decisions and behavior.

11D9ECAD773F459CAE19BDB424B6DBDC.description: Students identify ways to help and practice helping others at school, home, and other settings.

F47FF6946D834513850DD89FF506D0AD.description: Students understand acceptance versus exclusion and how they help or harm others.

109FFA2A3D8E441E9D132940834425B9.description: Students name people, places, and ideas that are important to them. Students can describe their own family traditions.

2BB069A2B3964D759E746CAB75C24667.description: Students recognize, label, and understand basic emotions in themselves and know that more than one emotion can be experienced at once. Students are aware of how emotions can affect their body.

59F79242AC2E47C7AF03BBD021287688.description: Students name their personal characteristics and life experiences and have an increasingly accurate basic sense of self. Students are aware of their own likes and dislikes.

standardSets.title: Self-Management: Adult
standardSets.subject: Transformative Social and Emotional Learning (T-SEL) Competencies (2020-)

document.title: T-SEL Competencies: Self-Management

430AE888FAD54A87AF6B65072A1ED20D.description: Adults model time management and organizational skills for their lives inside and outside of the learning environment.

ED76D306FBD74846812EA704E7AD50BB.description: Adults model strategies to identify their personal goals, evaluate their successes, modify their plans, and keep themselves motivated. Adults understand “paying attention” may look different based on culture and other aspects of student identity, including neurodiversity.

BFB45FBA0CC84487AE2BE513A045D3F1.description: Adults identify and articulate individual goals and demonstrate a variety of strategies to reach them. Adults model ways to work individually and collectively toward a common goal including using strategies such as establishing SMARTE goals.

6BB3401EE35D4824A5D326A2ACB4423F.description: Adults model the process of determining, expressing, and enforcing their own healthy boundaries. Adults respect others’ physical, social, emotional, and cultural boundaries.

8440D17E1D864CB6A0CC55B3A5CAECAC.description: Adults can receive and provide specific, contextually, and culturally appropriate constructive feedback. They listen to feedback from supervisors, peers, families, and students without defensiveness, assessing necessary changes and taking action to promote improvement.

65637683A0D84BB9AAEFAA4AFF193D93.description: Adults understand the science of adversity, how it interacts with systems of injustice, and the implications for supporting equitable student growth and development. Adults reflect on their own experiences of adversity and work to cultivate personal and collective resilience and a sense of hope in the learning environment and community.

FB5B3145A1B64023A1D71FF2C6F4211B.description: Adults observe and proactively manage stress by choosing appropriate stress management and self-care strategies that support their well-being. Adults identify and advocate for change when dysfunctional structures or unrealistic expectations are contributing to unmanageable stress.

489017F9CA2F429ABA5C48573E8AC9DB.description: Adults use a variety of culturally relevant practices to harness and regulate their emotions toward productive goals in contextually appropriate ways. Adults continuously work toward regulating strong and conflicting emotions and at sustaining joy.

standardSets.title: Transitional Kindergarten
standardSets.subject: Transitional Kindergarten California Common Core Standards (CCCS)

document.title: Transitional Kindergarten California Common Core Standards (CCCS)

5706A376C6204F4DB40CF51E52822A96.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

35C97B61E972460FBC402F1E70C1BEE6.description:
Describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and
